title.zh: 卷一百〇二 載記第二 劉聰
title.raw: 卷一百〇二 載記第二 劉聰 Volume 102 Records 2: Liu Cong

sentences.zh: 劉聰

translations.literal: Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 劉聰，字玄明，一名載，元海第四子也。

translations.literal: Liu Cong, courtesy name Xuanming, also called Zai, was the fourth son of Yuanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong, whose courtesy name was Xuanming and who was also known as Zai, was the fourth son of Liu Yuan (Yuanhai).

sentences.zh: 母曰張夫人。

translations.literal: His mother was titled Lady Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Zhang.

sentences.zh: 初，聰之在孕也，張氏夢日入懷，寤而以告，元海曰：「此吉徵也，慎勿言。

translations.literal: Initially, when Cong was in the womb, Lady Zhang dreamed that the sun entered her bosom; waking, she reported it, and Yuanhai said, "This is an auspicious omen; take care not to speak of it."
translations.idiomatic: While Cong was still in the womb, Lady Zhang dreamed that the sun slipped into her breast; when she woke and told Liu Yuan, he said, "That is a fortunate sign—but say nothing of it."

sentences.zh: 」十五月而生聰焉，夜有白光之異，形體非常。

translations.literal: " After fifteen months she gave birth to Cong; at night there was the anomaly of white light, and his physique was extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: " Fifteen months later she bore Cong; that night a strange white glow appeared, and the child’s physique was unlike any ordinary infant’s.

sentences.zh: 左耳有一白毫，長二尺餘，甚光澤。

translations.literal: In his left ear there was one white hair, more than two chi in length, very glossy.
translations.idiomatic: A single white hair more than two chi long grew from his left ear, bright and lustrous.

sentences.zh: 幼而聰悟好學，博士朱紀大奇之。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever, perceptive, and fond of learning; Erudite Zhu Ji greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was bright, quick to understand, and eager to learn; the court scholar Zhu Ji regarded him as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 年十四，究通經史，兼綜百家之言，《孫吳兵法》靡不誦之。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he had thoroughly penetrated the Classics and histories, and had also synthesized the doctrines of the hundred schools; there was none of the Sun and Wu military texts that he did not recite from memory.
translations.idiomatic: By fourteen he had mastered the canonical texts and histories and pulled together learning from every school; he knew every line of the military writings of Sun Wu by heart.

sentences.zh: 工草隸，善屬文，著述懷詩百餘篇、賦頌五十餘篇。

translations.literal: He was skilled in cursive and clerical scripts, adept at composing texts, and wrote more than a hundred reflective poems and more than fifty fu and encomia.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at cursive and clerical calligraphy, wrote polished prose, and left behind over a hundred reflective poems and more than fifty rhapsodies and laudatory pieces.

sentences.zh: 十五習擊刺，猿臂善射，彎弓三百斤，膂力驍捷，冠絕一時。

translations.literal: At fifteen he practiced thrusting and striking; he had ape-like arms and excelled at archery, could draw a bow of three hundred jin, and his strength and daring agility were foremost in his generation.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he trained in spear thrusts and swordplay; long-armed and a superb bowman, he could bend a bow rated at three hundred jin, and his raw strength and swift daring had no peer in his day.

sentences.zh: 太原王渾見而悅之，謂元海曰：「此兒吾所不能測也。」

translations.literal: Wang Hun of Taiyuan saw him and was pleased, saying to Yuanhai, "This boy is what I cannot fathom."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun of Taiyuan took one look and was delighted; he told Liu Yuan, "This son of yours is beyond my powers to measure."

sentences.zh: 弱冠游于京師，名士莫不交結，樂廣、張華尤異之也。

translations.literal: At his capping he traveled in the capital; there was no eminent gentleman with whom he did not forge ties, and Yue Guang and Zhang Hua regarded him as especially remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: After he came of age he moved among the elite of Luoyang; every notable scholar sought his acquaintance, and men such as Yue Guang and Zhang Hua singled him out as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 新興太守郭頤辟為主簿，舉良將，入為驍騎別部司馬，累遷右部都尉，善於撫接，五部豪右無不歸之。

translations.literal: The prefect of Xinxing, Guo Yi, summoned him as chief clerk; he was recommended as an able general, entered service as separate-command marshal of the fierce cavalry, and was repeatedly promoted to commandant of the right division; he was skilled in comforting and receiving people, and there was no magnate among the five divisions who did not attach himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi, governor of Xinxing, appointed him chief clerk and nominated him as a promising commander; he rose through the ranks to marshal of an independent column of crack horsemen and eventually commandant of the western tribes’ right wing. He had a gift for winning men over, and the powerful families of the five Xiongnu divisions all rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒表為赤沙中郎將。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, memorialized to appoint him general of the Gentlemen of the Household in Chisha.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, had him recommended as a gentleman-general stationed at Chisha.

sentences.zh: 聰以元海在鄴，懼為成都王穎所害，乃亡奔成都王，拜右積弩將軍，參前鋒戰事。

translations.literal: Cong, because Yuanhai was at Ye, feared he would be harmed by Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying; therefore he fled to join Prince of Chengdu, was appointed general of the household rapid crossbowmen on the right, and participated in vanguard military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that his father Liu Yuan, then at Ye, might fall victim to the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, Liu Cong fled into Ying’s camp instead; Ying named him a commander of the elite crossbow corps on the right and put him on the staff managing the forward armies.

sentences.zh: 元海為北單于，立為右賢王，隨還右部。

translations.literal: When Yuanhai became Northern Chanyu, he established him as Wise King of the Right and followed in returning to the right division.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuan assumed the title of Northern Chanyu, he installed Liu Cong as the Wise King of the Right and brought him back with the tribal host to their western homeland.

sentences.zh: 及即大單于位，更拜鹿蠡王。

translations.literal: When he assumed the great Chanyu position, he was further appointed Luli king.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yuan took the supreme title of Chanyu, Liu Cong was promoted to the rank of Luli king.

sentences.zh: 既殺其兄和，群臣勸即尊位。

translations.literal: Having killed his elder brother He, the assembled ministers urged him to assume the exalted position.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had disposed of his elder brother Liu He, his officials pressed him to mount the throne.

sentences.zh: 聰初讓其弟北海王乂，乂與公卿泣涕固請，聰久而許之，曰：「乂及群公正以四海未定，禍難尚殷，貪孤年長故耳。

translations.literal: Cong at first yielded to his younger brother Prince of Beihai Yi; Yi together with the dukes and ministers wept and firmly requested; after long time Cong consented, saying, "Yi and the assembled gentlemen simply because the four seas are not settled and disasters still abundant, covet my greater age, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: At first Liu Cong tried to yield the throne to his younger brother Liu Yi, Prince of Beihai; Yi and the senior ministers wept and refused to accept until, after prolonged pleading, Liu Cong relented and said, "You urge me only because the realm is still unsettled and calamities heap upon one another—and because I happen to be the elder brother."

sentences.zh: 此國家之事，孤敢不祗從。

translations.literal: This is a matter of state; how dare I not respectfully comply.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty itself is at stake, how could I refuse what you ask?"

sentences.zh: 今便欲遠遵魯隱，待乂年長，復子明辟。

translations.literal: Now I wish far to follow Duke Yin of Lu, waiting until Yi is grown in years, then restoring the son’s bright abdication.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to follow the ancient precedent of Duke Yin of Lu: hold power only until Yi comes of age, then restore the succession to him in due form."

sentences.zh: 」於是以僭即皇帝位，大赦境內，改元光興。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he usurped and assumed the emperor position, greatly pardoned within the borders, and changed the era name to Guangxing.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he took the imperial title—however illegitimate—issued a general amnesty throughout his domains, and proclaimed the era name Guangxing.

sentences.zh: 尊元海妻單氏曰皇太后，其母張氏為帝太后，乂為皇太弟，領大單于、大司徒，立其妻呼延氏為皇后，封其子粲為河內王，署使持節、撫軍大將軍、都督中外諸軍事，易河間王，翼彭城王，悝高平王。

translations.literal: He honored Yuanhai’s wife Lady Shan as empress dowager, his mother Lady Zhang as imperial dowager, Yi as imperial younger brother, concurrently holding great Chanyu and grand steward; he established his wife Lady Huyan as empress, enfeoffed his son Can as prince of Henei, appointed him bearer of credentials, general who comforts the army, area commander-in-chief of all military affairs within and without, Yi as prince of Hejian, Yi as prince of Pengcheng, Kui as prince of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He elevated Liu Yuan’s widow, Lady Shan, to empress dowager and his own mother, Lady Zhang, to dowager empress; he named Liu Yi heir presumptive as imperial younger brother while letting him retain the titles of great Chanyu and grand steward; he took Lady Huyan as empress and invested his son Liu Can as Prince of Henei with full credentials as commander who comforts the armies and director of all forces at court and in the field. Younger sons were ennobled as Liu Yi, Prince of Hejian; Liu Yi, Prince of Pengcheng; and Liu Kui, Prince of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 遣粲及其征東王彌、龍驤劉曜等率眾四萬，長驅入洛川，遂出轘轅，周旋梁、陳、汝、潁之間，陷壘壁百餘。

translations.literal: He dispatched Can together with his eastern campaign commander Wang Mi, Dragon-soaring general Liu Yao, and others leading a host of forty thousand; they drove straight into the Luoyang river basin, then emerged at Huanyuan, ranged between Liang, Chen, Ru, and Ying, and captured over a hundred fortified camps.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Liu Can with Wang Mi, who commanded the eastern front, and Liu Yao, general of the Dragon-Soaring guards—forty thousand men in all—on a deep thrust into the Luoyang basin; they burst through the Huanyuan pass and swept across the lands between Liang, Chen, the Ru, and the Ying, reducing more than a hundred Jin stockades.

sentences.zh: 以其司空劉景為大司馬，左光祿劉殷為大司徒，右光祿王育為大司空。

translations.literal: He appointed his minister of works Liu Jing grand marshal, left Household Rapid Liu Yin grand steward, and right Household Rapid Wang Yu minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Liu Jing from minister of works to grand marshal, named Liu Yin of the Household Rapid Horse on the left as grand steward, and Wang Yu of the Household Rapid Horse on right as chief minister of public works.

sentences.zh: 偽太后單氏姿色絕麗，聰蒸焉。

translations.literal: The bogus empress dowager Lady Shan’s appearance was surpassingly beautiful, and Cong committed upward marriage with her.
translations.idiomatic: The woman Jin still recognised as empress dowager, Lady Shan, was famously lovely; Liu Cong took her to his bed—a liaison counted as incest by Han ritual norms.

sentences.zh: 單即乂之母也，乂屢以為言，單氏慚恚而死，聰悲悼無已。

translations.literal: Shan was Yi’s mother; Yi repeatedly spoke about it; Lady Shan, ashamed and resentful, died, and Cong mourned without end.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shan was Liu Yi’s mother; Yi protested again and again until she died of shame and grief; Liu Cong mourned her obsessively.

sentences.zh: -{后}-知其故，乂之寵因此漸衰，然猶追念單氏，未便黜廢。

translations.literal: The empress understood the reason; Yi’s favor thereby gradually declined, yet still he cherished Lady Shan in memory and did not immediately degrade and discard her.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Huyan understood full well what had happened, and Liu Yi’s standing at court ebbed away—but Liu Cong still clung to memories of Lady Shan and stopped short of stripping her posthumous honours.

sentences.zh: 又尊母為皇太后。

translations.literal: Again he honored his mother as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He also elevated his own mother to the rank of empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 署其衛尉呼延晏為使持節、前鋒大都督、前軍大將軍。

translations.literal: He appointed his chamberlain for the palace garrison Huyan Yan bearer of credentials, grand area commander of the vanguard, and general-in-chief of the forward army.
translations.idiomatic: He named his minister of the guards, Huyan Yan, supreme commander of the forward armies with full imperial credentials.

sentences.zh: 配禁兵二萬七千，自宜陽入洛川，命王彌、劉曜及鎮軍石勒進師會之。

translations.literal: He assigned twenty-seven thousand forbidden troops, entering the Luoyang river basin from Yiyang, and ordered Wang Mi, Liu Yao, and garrison general Shi Le to advance their armies and join him.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-seven thousand palace guards marched with him from Yiyang into the Luoyang basin while Wang Mi, Liu Yao, and the independent commander Shi Le were ordered to bring their columns into the same theatre.

sentences.zh: 晏比及河南，王師前後十二敗，死者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: By the time Yan reached Henan, imperial armies had twelve successive defeats, with more than thirty thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: Before Yan even cleared Henan, Jin armies had lost twelve consecutive engagements and left thirty thousand corpses on the field.

sentences.zh: 彌等未至，晏留輜重于張方故壘，遂寇洛陽，攻陷平昌門，焚東陽、宣陽諸門及諸府寺。

translations.literal: Before Mi and the others arrived, Yan left baggage trains at Zhang Fang’s old fort, then raided Luoyang, stormed Pingchang Gate, and burned Dongyang, Xuanyang gates and various offices.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi’s reinforcements had not yet arrived when Yan parked his supply train at Zhang Fang’s abandoned camp, struck Luoyang itself, broke through Pingchang Gate, and set the Dongyang and Xuanyang gates ablaze along with whole blocks of government offices.

sentences.zh: 懷帝遣河南尹劉默距之，王師敗於社門。

translations.literal: Emperor Huai dispatched Henan intendant Liu Mo to resist him; imperial armies were defeated at She Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai ordered Liu Mo, governor of Henan, to hold the line, but Jin troops were routed at She Gate.

sentences.zh: 晏以外繼不至，出自東陽門，掠王公已下子女二百餘人而去。

translations.literal: Yan because outer reinforcements did not arrive, went out from Dongyang Gate, plundered more than two hundred sons and daughters from kings and dukes downward, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no relief columns, Yan slipped out through Dongyang Gate, dragged off more than two hundred noble women and children, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時帝將濟河東遁，具船于洛水，晏盡焚之，還于張方故壘。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was about to cross the river eastward and flee; boats were prepared on the Luo River; Yan burned them all and returned to Zhang Fang’s old fort.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had boats readied on the Luo for an escape across the Yellow River; Yan burned every hull and pulled back to Zhang Fang’s old earthworks.

sentences.zh: 王彌、劉曜至，復與晏會圍洛陽。

translations.literal: Wang Mi and Liu Yao arrived, again joined Yan and besieged Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mi and Liu Yao finally arrived, they linked up with Yan for a full siege of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時城內饑甚，人皆相食，百官分散，莫有固志。

translations.literal: At that time inside the city famine was extreme; people all ate one another; hundred officials scattered; none had firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the walls starvation had driven men to cannibalism; officials fled their posts; no one still believed the city could hold.

sentences.zh: 宣陽門陷，彌、晏入於南宮，升太極前殿，縱兵大掠，悉收宮人、珍寶。

translations.literal: Xuanyang Gate fell; Mi and Yan entered the southern palace, ascended the front hall of Taiji, unleashed troops to plunder greatly, and seized all palace women and treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyang Gate gave way; Wang Mi and Huyan Yan poured into the southern palace, climbed the steps of the Taiji Hall, turned their soldiers loose to loot, and swept up every concubine and heirloom they could find.

sentences.zh: 曜於是害諸王公及百官已下三萬餘人，于洛水北築為京觀。

translations.literal: Yao thereupon killed various kings and dukes and officials below numbering more than thirty thousand people, and north of the Luo River built them into a victory mound.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao then massacred thirty thousand Jin nobles and ministers and piled their corpses into a trophy mound on the north bank of the Luo.

sentences.zh: 遷帝及惠帝羊-{后}-、傳國六璽於平陽。

translations.literal: They moved the emperor and Emperor Hui’s Lady Yang empress and the six succession seals to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: They shipped Emperor Huai, Empress Yang—widow of Emperor Hui—and the six dynastic seals off to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 聰大赦，改年嘉平，以帝為特進、左光祿大夫、平阿公。

translations.literal: Cong greatly pardoned, changed the year to Jiaping, and appointed the emperor specially advanced, left Household Rapid grandee, duke of Ping’a.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong proclaimed a general amnesty, adopted the reign title Jiaping, and reduced the Jin sovereign to the hollow honour of senior adviser, grandee of the Household Rapid on the left, and Duke of Ping’a.

sentences.zh: 遣其平西趙染、安西劉雅率騎二萬攻南陽王模于長安，粲、曜率大眾繼之。

translations.literal: He dispatched his pacification-west Zhao Ran and pacification-west Liu Ya leading twenty thousand cavalry to attack Prince of Nanyang Mo at Chang’an; Can and Yao led great masses following them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhao Ran and Liu Ya westward at the head of twenty thousand horsemen to strike Sima Mo, the Prince of Nanyang, in Chang’an; Liu Can and Liu Yao followed with the main host.

sentences.zh: 染敗王師于潼關，將軍呂毅死之。

translations.literal: Ran defeated imperial armies at Tong Pass; general Lu Yi died in it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ran shattered the Jin army at Tong Pass; General Lu Yi fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 軍至於下邽，模乃降染。

translations.literal: When the army reached Xia Gui, Mo then surrendered to Ran.
translations.idiomatic: When the column reached Xia Gui, Sima Mo capitulated to Zhao Ran.

sentences.zh: 染送模於粲，粲害模及其子范陽王黎，送衛將軍梁芬、模長史魯繇、兼散騎常侍杜驁、辛謐及北宮純等於平陽。

translations.literal: Ran sent Mo to Can; Can harmed Mo and his son Prince of Fanyang Li, and sent guard general Liang Fen, Mo’s chief clerk Lu You, concurrent cavalry attendant Du Ao, Xin Mi, and Bei Gong Chun and others to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ran forwarded Sima Mo to Liu Can, who executed him together with his son Sima Li, Prince of Fanyang; Liang Fen, Lu You, Du Ao, Xin Mi, Bei Gong Chun, and other captured officers were marched to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 聰以粲之害模也，大怒。

translations.literal: Cong because of Can’s harming Mo was greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong flew into a rage when he learned Liu Can had killed Sima Mo.

sentences.zh: 粲曰：「臣殺模本不以其晚識天命之故，但以其晉氏肺腑，洛陽之難不能死節，天下之惡一也，故誅之。

translations.literal: Can said, "Your servant killed Mo originally not because he lately recognized Heaven’s mandate, but because he was Jin clan inner flesh; at Luoyang’s disaster he could not die for integrity—one with the world’s evil—therefore executed him."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can replied, "I executed Sima Mo not because he belatedly acknowledged Heaven’s will, but because he was bone of the Sima house yet refused to die honourably during the Luoyang catastrophe—making him as guilty as any traitor alive."

sentences.zh: 」聰曰：「雖然，吾恐汝不免誅降之殃也。

translations.literal: " Cong said, "Although so, I fear you will not escape the calamity of executing one who surrendered."
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Cong answered, "Even so, I suspect you have invited the curse that falls on those who butcher men who have already yielded."

sentences.zh: 夫天道至神，理無不報。」

translations.literal: Heaven’s way is supremely spirit-like; in principle nothing goes unrequited."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s accounting is subtle—no deed escapes its reckoning."

sentences.zh: 署劉曜為車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、雍州牧，改封中山王，鎮長安，王彌為大將軍，封齊公。

translations.literal: He appointed Liu Yao chariot-and-cavalry grand general, opening office with ceremonies equal to the three dukes, Yongzhou shepherd, changed enfeoffment to prince of Zhongshan, garrisoned Chang’an; Wang Mi as grand general, enfeoffed duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He confirmed Liu Yao as commander-in-chief of chariots and horse, with charter privileges matching the three highest ministers, governor of Yongzhou, and Prince of Zhongshan, stationed at Chang’an; Wang Mi became grand general and Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 尋而石勒等殺彌於己吾而並其眾，表彌叛狀。

translations.literal: Soon Shi Le and others killed Mi at Yiwu and annexed his masses, memorializing Mi’s rebellion circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Shi Le ambushed Wang Mi at Yiwu, absorbed his troops, and memorialised the court accusing Wang Mi of treason.

sentences.zh: 聰大怒，遣使讓勒專害公輔，有無上之心，又恐勒之有二志也，以彌部眾配之。

translations.literal: Cong was greatly angry, dispatched envoys to reproach Le for specially harming grand ministers, having heart without submitting upward, and also feared Le had two minds; he assigned Mi’s tribal masses to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong exploded with anger and sent envoys to rebuke Shi Le for murdering a pillar of state—proof, he said, of regicidal ambition—yet, wary that Shi Le might turn coat, he formally handed him Wang Mi’s soldiers.

sentences.zh: 劉曜既據長安，安定太守賈疋及諸氐羌皆送質任，唯雍州刺史麹特、新平太守竺恢固守不降。

translations.literal: Once Liu Yao had occupied Chang’an, Anding prefect Jia Ya and various Di and Qiang all sent hostages and appointments; only Yongzhou inspector Qu Te and Xinping prefect Zhu Hui firmly defended and did not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yao seized Chang’an, Jia Ya of Anding and the Di and Qiang leaders all sent hostages; only Qu Te, Jin’s inspector of Yongzhou, and Zhu Hui, prefect of Xinping, refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 護軍麹允、頻陽令梁肅自京兆南山將奔安定，遇疋任子于陰密，擁還臨涇，推疋為平南將軍，率眾五萬，攻曜于長安，扶風太守梁綜及麹特、竺恢等亦率眾十萬會之。

translations.literal: Protector-general Qu Yun and Pin-yang magistrate Liang Su from Jingzhao southern mountains were about to flee to Anding; meeting Ya’s hostage son at Yinmi, they escorted him back to Linjing, pushed Ya as pacification-south general, led a host of fifty thousand, attacked Yao at Chang’an; Fufeng prefect Liang Zong and Qu Te, Zhu Hui and others also led a host of one hundred thousand and joined them.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun and Liang Su had been retreating toward Anding from the Zhongnan slopes when they intercepted Jia Ya’s son near Yinmi; swinging back to Linjing, they proclaimed Jia Ya pacification general of the south and marched fifty thousand men against Liu Yao at Chang’an. Liang Zong of Fufeng, Qu Te, Zhu Hui, and others brought another hundred thousand to the rendezvous.

sentences.zh: 曜遣劉雅、趙染來距，敗績而還。

translations.literal: Yao dispatched Liu Ya and Zhao Ran to come oppose; they returned after defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao sent Liu Ya and Zhao Ran to intercept them but both generals limped back in defeat.

sentences.zh: 曜又盡長安銳卒與諸軍戰于黃丘，曜眾大敗，中流矢，退保甘渠。

translations.literal: Yao again exhausted Chang’an’s crack troops to battle the various armies at Huangqiu; Yao’s masses were greatly defeated, was struck by a flowing arrow, retreated and guarded Ganqu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao next threw every elite regiment left in Chang’an against the coalition at Huangqiu; his army collapsed, he himself took an arrow in the melee, and fled to fortify Ganqu.

sentences.zh: 杜人王禿、紀特等攻劉粲于新豐，粲還平陽。

translations.literal: Du men Wang Tu, Ji Te and others attacked Liu Can at Xinfeng; Can returned to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tu and Ji Te of Du county struck Liu Can at Xinfeng and forced him back to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 曜攻陷池陽，掠萬餘人歸於長安。

translations.literal: Yao attacked and took Chiyang, plundered more than ten thousand people and returned to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao stormed Chiyang, dragged off ten thousand captives, and withdrew into Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 時閻鼎等奉秦王為皇太子，入于雍城，關中戎晉莫不回應。

translations.literal: At that time Yan Ding and others upheld Prince of Qin as imperial heir apparent, entered Yong city; Guanzhong Rong and Jin none did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Yan Ding enthroned Sima Ye, the Prince of Qin, as heir apparent at Yongcheng, and every Jin loyalist and tribal ally in Guanzhong rallied to the banner.

sentences.zh: 聰-{后}-呼延氏死，將納其太保劉殷女，其弟乂固諫。

translations.literal: Cong empress Lady Huyan died; he was about to take in his grand guardian Liu Yin’s daughters; his younger brother Yi firmly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Huyan died, Liu Cong planned to marry daughters of his grand guardian Liu Yin; Prince Liu Yi protested vehemently.

sentences.zh: 聰更訪之于太宰劉延年、大傅劉景，景等皆曰：「臣常聞太保自云周劉康公之後，與聖氏本源既殊，納之為允。

translations.literal: Cong further enquired of grand tutor Liu Yannian and grand mentor Liu Jing; Jing and all said, "Your servants often heard the grand guardian himself say he was descended from Liu Kang-gong of Zhou; with the sage clan root origin already different, taking them in is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong polled Liu Yannian, senior tutor, and Liu Jing, senior mentor; Liu Jing replied for them all: "The grand guardian himself traces his line to Duke Kang of Zhou’s Liu—the bloodline diverges long ago from Your Majesty’s imperial house, so the marriages raise no ritual offence."

sentences.zh: 」聰大悅，使其兼大鴻臚李弘拜殷二女為左右貴嬪，位在昭儀上。

translations.literal: " Cong was greatly pleased, ordered his concurrent grand herald Li Hong to invest Yin’s two daughters as left and right noble concubines, rank above shining companion.
translations.idiomatic: " Delighted, Liu Cong ordered Li Hong, who doubled as minister of imperial audiences, to elevate two of Liu Yin’s daughters to senior concubines of the left and right, outranking even the "Shining Deportment" consorts.

sentences.zh: 又納殷女孫四人為貴人，位次貴嬪。

translations.literal: Again he took Yin’s granddaughters four persons as honoured ladies, rank following noble concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Four granddaughters of Liu Yin were brought in as honoured ladies just below those senior concubines.

sentences.zh: 謂弘曰：「此女輩皆姿色超世，女德冠時，且太保於朕實自不同，卿意安乎？

translations.literal: He said to Hong, "These women’s kind all have appearance surpassing the age, womanly virtue crowning the times; moreover the grand guardian toward Us is truly not the same—are you at ease in mind?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked Li Hong, "Every one of these girls combines incomparable beauty with virtue unmatched in our day; moreover Liu Yin and I are hardly kin in the ritual sense—does that set your mind at ease?"

sentences.zh: 」弘曰：「太保胤自有周，與聖源實別，陛下正以姓同為恨耳。

translations.literal: " Hong said, "The grand guardian’s descendants come from Zhou themselves; with the sage source truly distinct; Your Majesty only takes identical surname as regret."
translations.idiomatic: " Li Hong answered, "His pedigree begins with Zhou; it diverges cleanly from your own sacred line—Your Majesty hesitates only because the surname Liu is shared."

sentences.zh: 且魏司空東萊王基當世大儒，豈不達禮乎！

translations.literal: Moreover Wei minister of works Wang Ji of Donglai was the age’s great Ru—could he not comprehend ritual!
translations.idiomatic: Recall Wang Ji of Donglai, Wei’s minister of works—the foremost scholar of his generation—did he not understand ritual?"

sentences.zh: 為子納司空太原王沈女，以其姓同而源異故也。

translations.literal: For his son he took minister of works Wang Shen of Taiyuan’s daughter, because although their surname was identical their source was different.
translations.idiomatic: He married his son to a daughter of Wang Shen of Taiyuan precisely because the families shared a surname yet sprang from different ancestors."

sentences.zh: 」聰大悅，賜弘黃金六十斤，曰：「卿當以此意諭吾子弟輩。

translations.literal: " Cong was greatly pleased, bestowed on Hong sixty jin of gold, saying, "You ought with this meaning instruct Our sons and younger brothers."
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Cong rewarded Li Hong with sixty jin of gold and said, "Repeat this argument to my kinsmen until they understand."

sentences.zh: 」於是六劉之寵傾于後宮，聰稀復出外，事皆中黃門納奏，左貴嬪決之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the six Lius’ favour tipped the rear palace; Cong rarely again went out; affairs all had palace attendants submit memorials, left noble concubine decided them.
translations.idiomatic: " Henceforth the six Liu ladies dominated the inner palace; Liu Cong seldom emerged from it; eunuchs relayed every memorial, and the senior concubine on the left handed down the rulings.

sentences.zh: 聰假懷帝儀同三司，封會稽郡公，庾瑉等以次加秩。

translations.literal: Cong falsely invested Emperor Huai with ceremonies equal to the three dukes, enfeoffed him duke of Kuaiji commandery; Yu Min and others were promoted in rank in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong conferred ceremonial parity with the three dukes on the captive Jin emperor, created him Duke of Kuaiji, and bumped men such as Yu Min through successive sinecures.

sentences.zh: 聰引帝入宴，謂帝曰：「卿為豫章王時，朕嘗與王武子相造，武子示朕於卿，卿言聞其名久矣。

translations.literal: Cong led the emperor into a banquet, saying to the emperor, "When you were Prince of Yuzhang, We once with Wang Wuzi paid mutual visits; Wuzi showed Us to you; you said you had heard his name long."
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet Liu Cong led Emperor Huai in and said, "When you were Prince of Yuzhang, I once visited Wang Ji—Wang Ji introduced me to you, and you told me you had admired his reputation for years."

sentences.zh: 以卿所制樂府歌示朕，謂朕曰：'聞君善為辭賦，試為看之。

translations.literal: He showed Us the Music Bureau songs you composed, saying to Us: 'I hear you are skilled at composing fu; try writing some for viewing.'
translations.idiomatic: He showed me the yuefu lyrics you had written and said, ‘They say you excel at rhapsodies—write something for us to judge.’

sentences.zh: '朕時與武子俱為《盛德頌》，卿稱善者久之。

translations.literal: ' At that time We together with Wuzi both composed 'Ode to Lofty Virtue'; you praised it well for long.
translations.idiomatic: ‘That day Wang Ji and I both presented our “Odes on Lofty Virtue,” and you pronounced them excellent again and again.’

sentences.zh: 又引朕射於皇堂，朕得十二籌，卿與武子俱得九籌，卿贈朕柘弓、銀研，卿頗憶否？

translations.literal: Again he led Us to shoot in the imperial hall; We obtained twelve tallies, you and Wuzi both obtained nine tallies; you presented Us with a mulberry bow and silver inkstone—do you quite recall?
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Ji led us to the imperial archery hall: I myself scored twelve hits while you and Wang Ji each scored nine; afterwards you presented me with a mulberry bow and a silver inkstone—do you remember any of that?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「臣安敢忘之，但恨爾日不早識龍顏。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Your servant how dare forget it, only regrets that day not early recognizing dragon countenance."
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Huai replied, "How could I forget—only I regret that I did not then recognise Your Majesty’s dragon face."

sentences.zh: 」聰曰：「卿家骨肉相殘，何其甚也？

translations.literal: " Cong said, "Your clan flesh and bone mutually injure—how extreme!"
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Cong asked, "Why did your own kin tear one another apart so savagely?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「此殆非人事，皇天之意也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "This probably is not human affair; it is August Heaven’s intention."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor answered, "That was scarcely of men’s doing—it was Heaven’s decree."

sentences.zh: 大漢將應乾受曆，故為陛下自相驅除。

translations.literal: Great Han will respond to Qian and receive the calendar; therefore for Your Majesty they mutually drive out and remove.
translations.idiomatic: The great Han is destined to receive the mandate; your majesty’s house simply cleared the path on its own."

sentences.zh: 且臣家若能奉武皇之業，九族敦睦，陛下何由得之！

translations.literal: Moreover if your servant’s clan could uphold Martial Emperor’s enterprise, nine kinlets warmly harmonious—how would Your Majesty obtain it!
translations.idiomatic: Had my family preserved Emperor Wu’s legacy and kept the nine branches at peace, how could Your Majesty ever have seized it!"

sentences.zh: 」至日夕乃出，以小劉貴人賜帝，謂帝曰：「此名公之孫，今特以相妻，卿宜善遇之。

translations.literal: " Until dusk then he came out, bestowing on the emperor the younger Lady Liu honoured lady, saying to the emperor, "This is a famed grandee’s granddaughter; now specially to be your wife; you ought treat her well."
translations.idiomatic: " Only at dusk did Liu Cong dismiss him, handing over the junior Lady Liu with the words, "She is the granddaughter of a celebrated minister; I give her to you as consort—cherish her."

sentences.zh: 」拜劉為會稽國夫人。

translations.literal: " He invested Liu as lady of Kuaiji state.
translations.idiomatic: " She was invested as consort of the Kuaiji princedom.

sentences.zh: 遣其鎮北靳沖寇太原，平北卜珝率眾繼之。

translations.literal: He dispatched his garrison-north Jin Chong to raid Taiyuan; pacification-north Bu Xu led masses following him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jin Chong, general who guards the north, to raid Taiyuan while Bu Xu, pacification general of the north, followed with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 沖攻太原不克，而歸罪於珝，輒斬之。

translations.literal: Chong attacked Taiyuan without taking it, but attributed guilt to Xu and summarily beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Chong failed to storm Taiyuan, blamed Bu Xu for the setback, and executed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 聰聞之，大怒曰：「此人朕所不得加刑，沖何人哉！

translations.literal: Cong hearing it was greatly angry and said, "This person is one on whom We could not impose punishment—what kind of man is Chong!"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Cong heard the news he thundered, "Even I would not lightly punish that man—who is Jin Chong to strike him down!"

sentences.zh: 」遣其御史中丞浩衍持節斬沖。

translations.literal: " He dispatched his imperial secretary supervisor Hao Yan bearing credentials to behead Chong.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Hao Yan, chief of the censorate, with imperial insignia to execute Jin Chong.

sentences.zh: 左都水使者襄陵王攄坐魚蟹不供，將作大匠望都公靳陵坐溫明、徽光二殿不成，皆斬於東市。

translations.literal: Left director of waters Prince Xiangling Shu sat because fish and crabs were not supplied; chief artisan Duke of Wangdu Jin Ling sat because Warm Bright and Radiant Sign two halls were not completed; all were beheaded at eastern market.
translations.idiomatic: Sim Shu, Prince of Xiangling and superintendent of waterways, went to the block for failing to deliver fish and shellfish; Jin Ling, Duke of Wangdu and minister of public works, died for leaving the Warm Bright and Radiant Sign halls unfinished—both executions took place in the eastern marketplace.

sentences.zh: 聰游獵無度，常晨出暮歸，觀漁于汾水，以燭繼晝。

translations.literal: Cong hunted and roamed without measure, often morning out evening returning, watched fishing on Fen River, used candles to continue daytime.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong hunted without restraint, riding out at dawn and returning only after dark; he idled by the Fen watching fishermen haul nets and carried the revelry on by candlelight as though daylight never ended.

sentences.zh: 中軍王彰諫曰：「今大難未夷，余晉假息，陛下不懼白龍魚服之禍，而昏夜忘歸。

translations.literal: Central army Wang Zhang remonstrated saying, "Now great disaster not yet pacified, remnant Jin borrows breath; Your Majesty does not fear white dragon fish-clothes calamity, yet in dark night forgets return.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang of the central army warned him: "The great crisis is unfinished and Jin still draws breath; instead of fearing the fate of the dragon who walked among fish in mortal garb, you linger abroad night after night."

sentences.zh: 陛下當思先帝創業之艱難，嗣承之不易，鴻業已爾，四海屬情，何可墜之于垂成，隳之於將就！

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought think of former emperor’s founding enterprise’s hardship, succession’s not easy; great enterprise already thus, four seas attach feeling—how can let it fall at near completion, ruin it at about to succeed!
translations.idiomatic: Remember how painfully your father forged this realm and how fragile its succession remains; the great enterprise now hangs on you while the world watches—how can you dash it on the verge of success!"

sentences.zh: 比竊觀陛下所為，臣實痛心疾首有日矣。

translations.literal: Lately secretly observing Your Majesty’s conduct, your servant truly has been heart-pained and head-aching for days.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day I have watched your behaviour in secret, and my heart has burned with grief."

sentences.zh: 且愚人系漢之心未專，而思晉之懷猶盛，劉琨去此咫尺之間，狂狷刺客息頃而至。

translations.literal: Moreover foolish people’s tie to Han heart not yet concentrated, while longing for Jin’s bosom still abundant; Liu Kun is from here within a foot’s distance; unruly assassins in a breath’s moment arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The common folk still divide their loyalty between Han and Jin, and Liu Kun camps within a stone’s throw—any zealot with a dagger could reach you before guards blink."

sentences.zh: 帝王輕出，一夫敵耳。

translations.literal: Emperor-kings lightly go out—a single man is enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When an emperor wanders abroad without care, a lone assassin is weapon enough."

sentences.zh: 願陛下改往修來，則憶兆幸甚。

translations.literal: Wish Your Majesty reform past and cultivate future; then hundred millions extremely fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Turn from these ways and rule as you ought, and countless subjects will bless your name."

sentences.zh: 」聰大怒，命斬之。

translations.literal: " Cong was greatly angry, ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Cong erupted and ordered Wang Zhang executed.

sentences.zh: 上夫人王氏叩頭乞哀，乃囚之詔獄。

translations.literal: Upper lady Wang knocked head begging pity; then imprisoned him in imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang of the senior harem threw herself at his feet pleading mercy, so Liu Cong threw Wang Zhang into the imperial jail instead.

sentences.zh: 聰母以聰刑怒過差，三日不食，弟乂、子粲並與切諫。

translations.literal: Cong’s mother because Cong’s punishments anger exceeded measure, three days did not eat; younger brother Yi and son Can together earnestly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong’s mother stopped eating for three days to protest his violent rage; Prince Liu Yi and Crown Prince Liu Can joined her in blunt remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 聰怒曰：「吾豈桀、紂、幽、厲乎，而汝等生來哭人！

translations.literal: Cong angrily said, "Am I Jie, Zhou, You, Li—yet you lot born come weeping at people!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong snarled, "Do I look like Jie, Zhou, King You, or King Li—why must you nag me like mourners at a funeral!"

sentences.zh: 」其太宰劉延年及諸公卿列侯百有餘人，皆免冠涕泣固諫曰：「光文皇帝以聖武膺期，創建鴻祚，而六合未一，夙世升遐。

translations.literal: " His grand tutor Liu Yannian and various dukes and ministers and ranked marquises more than one hundred persons, all removed caps weeping and firmly remonstrated saying, "Emperor Guangwen by sagely martial received the period, founded great blessing, yet six directions not unified, early departed ascending far.
translations.idiomatic: " More than a hundred officers led by Grand Tutor Liu Yannian tore off their caps and wept: "Emperor Guangwen seized the mandate through sagely prowess and laid the foundations of your dynasty, yet he died before the realm was whole."

sentences.zh: 陛下睿德自天，龍飛紹統，東平洛邑，南定長安，真可謂功高周成，德超夏啟。

translations.literal: Your Majesty keen virtue from Heaven, dragon soaring continuing succession, east pacified Luoyi, south settled Chang’an—truly can be called merit higher than Zhou Cheng, virtue surpassing Xia Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rose by Heaven’s favour, restored the succession, crushed Luoyang in the east and Chang’an in the south—your achievements rival King Cheng of Zhou and your virtue outshines Qi of Xia."

sentences.zh: 往也唐虞，今則陛下，曆觀書記，未有此比。

translations.literal: In antiquity there were Tang and Yu; now there is Your Majesty; surveying documents and records, there has never been a parallel like this.
translations.idiomatic: The age of Tang and Yao lies in the past; today it is Your Majesty who holds the mirror of sage-kings—and nowhere in the annals do we find a ruler who matched what you have achieved.

sentences.zh: 而頃頻以小務不供而斬王公，直言忤旨，便囚大將，游獵無度，機管不修，臣等竊所未解，臣等所以破肝糜胃忘寢與食者也。

translations.literal: Yet lately, time and again, you executed kings and dukes over trifling shortages of supplies; straightforward counsel that offended you meant instant imprisonment for a leading general; you hunt without restraint and neglect the machinery of government—we cannot fathom it, and it is why we tear our hearts out and forget food and sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Yet of late trivial supply failures cost princes of the blood their heads; one blunt warning landed a field marshal in chains; hunts never end while state business moulders—we lie awake nights trying to understand why our sovereign acts thus.

sentences.zh: 」聰乃赦彰。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Cong pardoned Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Cong relented and spared Wang Zhang.

sentences.zh: 麹特等圍長安，劉曜連戰敗績，乃驅掠士女八萬餘口退還平陽，因攻司徒傅祗於三渚，使其右將軍劉參攻郭默於懷城。

translations.literal: Qu Te and others besieged Chang’an; Liu Yao suffered repeated defeats; he then drove off more than eighty thousand men and women as captives and withdrew to Pingyang, attacked Minister of Education Fu Di at Sanzhu, and ordered his general of the right Liu Shen to strike Guo Mo at Huai fortress.
translations.idiomatic: While Qu Te kept Chang’an under siege, Liu Yao lost battle after battle, swept eighty thousand souls back to Pingyang as booty, turned on Fu Di at Sanzhu, and detached Liu Shen to besiege Guo Mo in Huai.

sentences.zh: 祗病卒，城陷，遷祗孫純、粹並二萬餘戶於平陽縣。

translations.literal: Di died of illness; the city fell; Di’s grandsons Chun and Cui were relocated along with more than twenty thousand households into Pingyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Di died before the walls yielded; his grandsons Fu Chun and Fu Cui were marched north with twenty thousand households once the citadel capitulated.

sentences.zh: 聰贈祗太保，純、粹皆給事中，謂祗子暢曰：「尊公雖不達天命，然各忠其主，吾亦有以亮之。

translations.literal: Cong posthumously honoured Di as grand guardian; Chun and Cui were both appointed palace advisers. He told Di’s son Chang: “Though your honoured father never bowed to Heaven’s decree, each man owed loyalty to his own lord—I can respect that.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong awarded Fu Di the posthumous title of grand guardian, named Fu Chun and Fu Cui palace advisers, and told Fu Chang: “Your father refused our mandate, yet he remained faithful to Jin—I grant him that.”

sentences.zh: 但晉主已降，天命非人所支，而虔劉南鄙，沮亂邊萌，此其罪也。

translations.literal: But the Jin sovereign has already surrendered; the mandate is no longer theirs to uphold, yet Di butchered our southern marches and threw the frontier populations into chaos—that is his offence.
translations.idiomatic: The Sima emperor has yielded the throne; destiny cannot be propped up by mortal hands—yet Fu Di ravaged our southern borderlands and terrified the frontier folk. That is his guilt.

sentences.zh: 以元惡之種而贈同勳舊，逆臣之孫荷榮禁闥，卿知皇漢之德弘曠以不？

translations.literal: You treat the offspring of arch-villains like elders who earned their honours and let the grandsons of traitors shine inside the forbidden gates—do you grasp how vast is the virtue of imperial Han?”
translations.idiomatic: You heap honours on the bloodline of Jin’s worst ministers and let rebel spawn glitter within the palace—have you any idea how magnanimous our Han throne has already been?”

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「陛下每嘉先臣，不以小臣之故而虧其忠節，及是恩也，自是明主伐國吊人之義，臣輒同萬物，未敢謝生於自然。」

translations.literal: ” Chang said: “Your Majesty ever praises my late father and does not, on account of petty ministers, diminish his loyal honour—such grace is precisely what an enlightened lord shows when he conquers a state yet consoles its people. Your servant counts himself no more than another creature under Heaven and would not presume to mouth gratitude for being spared.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Fu Chang answered: “You praise my father’s loyalty without letting lesser men stain his name—that is the mercy that marks a true conqueror. I stand mute before such kindness; I would not insult it with hollow thanks.”

sentences.zh: 聰遣劉粲、劉曜等攻劉琨于晉陽，琨使張喬距之，戰于武灌，喬敗績，死之，晉陽危懼。

translations.literal: Cong dispatched Liu Can and Liu Yao and others to attack Liu Kun at Jinyang; Kun sent Zhang Qiao to oppose them; they fought at Wuguan; Qiao was routed and killed; Jinyang trembled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong sent Liu Can and Liu Yao against Liu Kun at Jinyang; Liu Kun committed Zhang Qiao to stop them at Wuguan, where Zhang died in rout and the city faced ruin.

sentences.zh: 太原太守高喬、琨別駕郝聿以晉陽降粲。

translations.literal: Taiyuan prefect Gao Qiao and Kun’s aide Hao Yu surrendered Jinyang to Can.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan’s governor Gao Qiao and Liu Kun’s aide Hao Yu opened Jinyang’s gates to Liu Can.

sentences.zh: 琨與左右數十騎，攜其妻子奔于趙郡之亭頭，遂如常山。

translations.literal: Kun with several dozen horsemen of his escort, carrying wife and children, fled to Tingtou in Zhao commandery, then proceeded to Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun escaped with a handful of riders, his family in tow, first to Tingtou in Zhao and then into the hills of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 粲、曜入于晉陽。

translations.literal: Can and Yao entered Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can and Liu Yao marched into Jinyang unopposed.

sentences.zh: 先是，琨與代王猗盧結為兄弟，乃告敗于猗盧，且乞師。

translations.literal: Earlier, Kun had sworn brotherhood with the Prince of Dai, Yilu; he now reported his defeat to Yilu and begged for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun had long sworn fellowship with Tuoba Yilu, prince of Dai; beaten and desperate, he appealed to him for an army.

sentences.zh: 猗盧遣子日利孫、賓六須及將軍衛雄、姬澹等率眾數萬攻晉陽，琨收散卒千餘為之鄉導，猗盧率眾六萬至於狼猛。

translations.literal: Yilu sent his sons Rilisun and Bin Liuxu and generals Wei Xiong and Ji Dan and others leading tens of thousands to strike Jinyang; Kun gathered more than a thousand scattered troops to guide them; Yilu himself brought sixty thousand warriors to Langmeng.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu dispatched tens of thousands under his sons Rilisun and Bin Liuxu and generals Wei Xiong and Ji Dan; Liu Kun scraped together a thousand survivors as scouts while Yilu closed in with sixty thousand horse from Langmeng.

sentences.zh: 曜及賓六須戰於汾東，曜墜馬，中流矢，身被七創。

translations.literal: Yao and Bin Liuxu fought east of the Fen; Yao fell from his horse, was struck by an arrow, and suffered seven wounds.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Fen, Liu Yao clashed with Bin Liuxu, was thrown from the saddle, took an arrow through the flesh, and counted seven separate wounds.

sentences.zh: 討虜傅武以馬授曜，曜曰：「當今危亡之極，人各思免。

translations.literal: Campaign commander Fu Wu offered his horse to Yao; Yao said: “We stand at the brink of ruin and everyone thinks only of saving himself.”
translations.idiomatic: Fu Wu, a minor commander, pressed his mount on Liu Yao, who answered: “The army is breaking—every man already thinks of flight.”

sentences.zh: 吾創已重，自分死此矣。

translations.literal: “My wounds are too grave; I expect to die here.”
translations.idiomatic: “These cuts go too deep—I am finished on this field.”

sentences.zh: 」武泣曰：「武小人，蒙大王識拔，以至於是，常思效命，今其時矣。

translations.literal: ” Wu wept and said: “Wu is a petty man whom the great king raised from nothing; I have burned to repay that debt—now is the hour.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Fu Wu wept: “You lifted me from dust; let me repay that debt now.”

sentences.zh: 且皇室始基，大難未弭，天下何可一日無大王也。

translations.literal: “Moreover the imperial house has barely laid its foundations and catastrophe still looms—how can the realm endure a single day without its great king!”
translations.idiomatic: “The dynasty is newborn and peril still stalks us—the state cannot lose you for even one dawn!”

sentences.zh: 」於是扶曜乘馬，驅令渡汾，回而戰死。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon they helped Yao onto the horse, drove him across the Fen, then wheeled about and died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: ” They hoisted Liu Yao onto the charger, forced it through the Fen, then turned back and died covering his retreat.

sentences.zh: 曜入晉陽，夜與劉粲等掠百姓，逾蒙山遁歸。

translations.literal: Yao entered Jinyang; in the night he and Liu Can and others plundered the populace, crossed Meng Mountain, and slipped away.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao slipped into Jinyang after dark, looted with Liu Can, crossed Mengshan by night, and fled south.

sentences.zh: 猗盧率騎追之，戰于藍穀，粲敗績，斬其征虜邢延，獲其鎮北劉豐。

translations.literal: Yilu led cavalry in pursuit; they fought at Langu; Can was routed; his campaign commander Xing Yan was beheaded; his garrison-north Liu Feng was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Yilu chased them to Langu, shattered Liu Can’s line, took Xing Yan’s head, and bagged Liu Feng, the northern garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 琨收合離散，保于陽曲，猗盧戍之而還。

translations.literal: Kun gathered the dispersed and held Yangqu; Yilu garrisoned it for him and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun rallied his fugitives at Yangqu; Yilu left troops to stiffen the defence and rode home.

sentences.zh: 正旦，聰宴於光極前殿，逼帝行酒，光祿大夫庾瑉、王俊等起而大哭，聰惡之。

translations.literal: At New Year dawn Cong held court feast in the forward hall of Radiant Apex and forced the Jin emperor to circulate the wine; Household Rapid grandees Yu Min and Wang Jun rose wailing; Cong took offence.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year’s morning Liu Cong feasted in the Guangji Hall and made Emperor Huai pour wine for his captors; Yu Min and Wang Jun burst into tears—an insult Liu Cong could not abide.

sentences.zh: 會有告瑉等謀以平陽應劉琨者，聰遂鴆帝而誅瑉、俊，復以賜帝劉夫人為貴人，大赦境內殊死已下。

translations.literal: Word arrived that Yu Min and others plotted to hand Pingyang to Liu Kun; Cong thereupon poisoned the emperor, executed Yu and Wang, elevated the Lady Liu previously given to the emperor to honoured-lady rank, and proclaimed amnesty for all crimes short of capital offences.
translations.idiomatic: When informers claimed Yu Min meant to surrender Pingyang to Liu Kun, Liu Cong poisoned the captive emperor, executed Yu and Wang, promoted the Liu lady he had married to Huai to chief concubine, and declared a general amnesty short of death sentences.

sentences.zh: 立左貴嬪劉氏為皇后。

translations.literal: He raised the left noble concubine, Lady Liu, to empress.
translations.idiomatic: He crowned Lady Liu, his senior concubine of the left, as empress.

sentences.zh: 聰將為劉氏起皇儀樓於後庭，廷尉陳元達諫曰：「臣聞古之聖王愛國如家，故皇天亦祐之如子。

translations.literal: Cong planned to erect for Lady Liu the Imperial Splendour Tower in the inner palace; Commandant of Justice Chen Yuanda remonstrated: “Your servant has heard that ancient sage-kings cherished the realm as their household—therefore High Heaven cherished them as sons.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong meant to build an Imperial Splendour Tower for Empress Liu; Chen Yuanda, chief justice, warned: “The sage-kings loved their people as family—only thus did Heaven love the throne.”

sentences.zh: 夫天生蒸民而樹之君者，使為之父母以刑賞之，不欲使殿屎黎元而蕩逸一人。

translations.literal: For Heaven creates the steaming multitude and sets a ruler over them so that he may be father and mother, wielding punishment and reward—not so that palaces may groan with suffering among the black-haired masses while one man abandons himself to pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven bred the people and gave them a sovereign to be mother and father, wielding reward and punishment—not so one ruler could lounge in jewelled halls while common folk groaned outside.

sentences.zh: 晉氏暗虐，視百姓如草芥，故上天剿絕其祚。

translations.literal: The Sima clan ruled in darkness and cruelty, treating the hundred surnames like straw; therefore High Heaven cut short their fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin treated subjects like weeds; Heaven erased their mandate.

sentences.zh: 乃眷皇漢，蒼生引領息肩，懷更蘇之望有日矣。

translations.literal: Then turning to imperial Han, the black-haired masses crane their necks for respite and have long nursed hopes of revival.
translations.idiomatic: Now they look to Han with upturned faces, praying for relief—the thirst for renewal has simmered for years.

sentences.zh: 我高祖光文皇帝靖言惟茲，痛心疾首，故身衣大布，居不重茵；

translations.literal: Our founding sovereign Emperor Guangwen pondered this alone and nursed a bitter ache; hence he wore coarse cloth himself and never layered mats beneath his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Our founding Emperor Guangwen burned with that burden—he wore hemp, refused double mats, and taught austerity by example.

sentences.zh: 先皇后嬪服無綺彩。

translations.literal: The late empress and concubines wore no embroidered silks.
translations.idiomatic: Even his consorts renounced brocade.

sentences.zh: 重逆群臣之請，故建南北宮焉。

translations.literal: Only because he yielded repeatedly to his ministers’ pleas did south and north palaces rise at all.
translations.idiomatic: Those twin palaces exist only because ministers wore him down.

sentences.zh: 今光極之前足以朝群后、饗萬國矣，昭德、溫明已後足可以容六宮、列十二等矣。

translations.literal: Today the court before Radiant Apex suffices to assemble the lords and feast the myriad domains; beyond Bright Virtue and Mild Splendour there is ample space for the six palaces and twelve ranks of ladies.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangji court already hosts the realm; halls such as Zhaode and Wenming hold the harem—nothing more is needed.

sentences.zh: 陛下龍興已來，外殄二京不世之寇，內興殿觀四十餘所，重之以饑饉疾疫，死亡相屬，兵疲於外，人怨於內，為之父母固若是乎！

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty mounted the dragon throne you have crushed rare foes at both capitals abroad while raising more than forty palace complexes within—added to famine and plague where death treads on death, armies exhausted in the field and hatred boiling at home—is this how fathers and mothers ought to rule?
translations.idiomatic: Since your accession you have razed both Jin capitals yet poured labour into forty new mansions while famine and plague stack corpses at the gates—troops stagger home empty-handed and the people curse your name. Is this guardianship?

sentences.zh: 伏聞詔旨，將營皇儀，中宮新立，誠臣等樂為子來者也。

translations.literal: Prostrate, we hear the edict intends to raise Imperial Splendour; the inner palace has a fresh mistress—indeed your servants would rejoice to labour like sons summoned to build her hall.
translations.idiomatic: We hear you mean to raise the Imperial Splendour Tower now that a new empress sits—we would gladly sweat like sons for her sake.

sentences.zh: 竊以大難未夷，宮宇粗給，今之所營，尤實非宜。

translations.literal: Yet your servant privately reflects that catastrophe is unfinished and palace space barely adequate; such construction now would be singularly ill-timed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet disaster still stalks us and existing halls suffice—another tower now would be folly.

sentences.zh: 臣聞太宗承高祖之業，惠呂息役之後，以四海之富，天下之殷，尚以百金之費而輟露臺，歷代垂美，為不朽之跡。

translations.literal: Your servant notes that Emperor Wen of Han inherited Gaozu’s work after the troubles of Empress Lü’s tyranny; though he commanded the wealth of the empire he halted the Dew Terrace over a mere hundred pieces of gold—later ages hymn that restraint as immortal wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Han Wendi: after Lü’s chaos he inherited a rich empire yet refused a terrace costing only a hundred gold pieces—posterity still sings of his restraint.

sentences.zh: 故能斷獄四百，擬于成康。

translations.literal: Hence he could reduce lawsuits to four hundred a year, rivalling the golden reigns of kings Cheng and Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Hence his courts heard barely four hundred cases a year—true kin to Cheng and Kang.

sentences.zh: 陛下之所有，不過太宗二郡地耳，戰守之備者，豈僅匈奴、南越而已哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty commands scarcely more territory than Emperor Wen’s two commanderies; the demands of defence extend far beyond Xiongnu and Southern Yue alone!
translations.idiomatic: You hold hardly more ground than Wendi’s twin basins, yet your defence burden dwarfs anything the Xiongnu or Southern Yue ever posed!

sentences.zh: 孝文之廣，思費如彼；

translations.literal: Emperor Wen’s breadth of mind shrank from expense even when prosperous;
translations.idiomatic: Wendi shrank from waste even in abundance;

sentences.zh: 陛下之狹，欲損如此。

translations.literal: Your Majesty’s narrow circumstance yet desires ruinous spending like this.
translations.idiomatic: you court extravagance on a shoestring.

sentences.zh: 愚臣所以敢昧死犯顏色，冒不測之禍者也。

translations.literal: That is why this foolish servant braves death and predictable wrath by speaking bluntly.”
translations.idiomatic: That is why I risk execution to say it aloud.”

sentences.zh: 」聰大怒曰：「吾為萬機主，將營一殿，豈問汝鼠子乎！

translations.literal: ” Cong flew into a rage: “We rule the myriad threads of state—shall we ask rats like you before raising one hall?”
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Cong snarled: “I govern the realm—since when does a rat dictate my roof?”

sentences.zh: 不殺此奴，沮亂朕心，朕殿何當得成邪！

translations.literal: “Unless this slave dies he will clog Our purpose—when shall Our hall ever rise!”
translations.idiomatic: “Kill him or lose the throne—choose!”

sentences.zh: 將出斬之，並其妻子同梟東市，使群鼠共穴。

translations.literal: He ordered the guards to drag Chen out for execution together with wife and children, expose their heads in the eastern market, and let the rats share one pit.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded guards to drag Chen Yuanda, his wife, and children to the eastern market for execution and gibbeting—“Let every rat share their grave.”

sentences.zh: 」時在逍遙園李中堂，元達抱堂下樹叫曰：「臣所言者，社稷之計也，而陛下殺臣。

translations.literal: ” At that moment in the Rambling Garden’s Li inner hall Yuanda clasped a courtyard tree and shouted: “Your servant spoke for the altars of soil and grain—yet Your Majesty murders him!”
translations.idiomatic: ” In the Li pavilion of Rambling Garden Chen Yuanda chained himself to a tree: “I spoke for the dynasty—and you kill me for it!”

sentences.zh: 若死者有知，臣要當上訴陛下于天，下訴陛下于先帝。

translations.literal: “If the dead retain awareness, your servant will indict Your Majesty before Heaven above and before the former emperor below.”
translations.idiomatic: “If spirits endure I shall accuse you before Heaven and before Emperor Guangwen himself.”

sentences.zh: 朱雲有云：『臣得與龍逢、比干游於地下足矣。

translations.literal: “Zhu Yun once said: ‘Better roam beneath the earth with Longfeng and Bigan.’”
translations.idiomatic: “Zhu Yun swore he would sooner walk the underworld with Gun and Bi Gan.”

sentences.zh: 』未審陛下何如主耳！

translations.literal: “Who then are you as sovereign!”
translations.idiomatic: “What sort of ruler does that make you?”

sentences.zh: 」元達先鎖腰而入，及至，即以鎖繞樹，左右曳之不能動。

translations.literal: ” Yuanda had entered with chains about his waist; once inside he looped them around the trunk so attendants could not drag him loose.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chen had entered in fetters; he snapped them around the trunk so guards could not haul him away.

sentences.zh: 聰怒甚。

translations.literal: Cong’s fury swelled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong’s rage boiled higher.

sentences.zh: 劉氏時在後堂，聞之，密遣中常侍私敕左右停刑，於是手疏切諫，聰乃解，引元達而謝之，易逍遙園為納賢園，李中堂為愧賢堂。

translations.literal: Lady Liu was in the rear hall; hearing the uproar she secretly sent a chief eunuch to halt the execution, then penned an urgent memorial herself until Cong relented, summoned Yuanda, apologised, renamed Rambling Garden “Garden for Welcoming Worthies,” and the Li hall “Hall Ashamed before Worthies.”
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu, listening from the inner chambers, sent eunuchs to stay the swords, drafted her own blistering protest, and shamed Liu Cong into freeing Chen, apologising, and renaming the garden and hall to honour honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 時湣帝即位于長安，聰遣劉曜及司隸喬智明、武牙李景年等寇長安，命趙染率眾赴之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min ascended at Chang’an, Cong dispatched Liu Yao together with metropolitan commander Qiao Zhiming and martial-fang guard Li Jingnian to raid the capital while Zhao Ran brought supporting troops.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Min took the throne in Chang’an, Liu Cong launched Liu Yao, Qiao Zhiming, and Li Jingnian against the city with Zhao Ran reinforcing them.

sentences.zh: 時大都督麹允據黃白城，累為曜、染所敗。

translations.literal: Grand commander Qu Yun held Huangbai fortress but Liu Yao and Zhao Ran defeated him again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun clung to Huangbai city yet Liu Yao and Zhao Ran broke him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 染謂曜曰：「麹允率大眾在外，長安可襲而取之。

translations.literal: Ran told Yao: “Qu Yun keeps the main host outside—Chang’an itself may be seized by surprise.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ran urged Liu Yao: “Qu Yun’s army is camped away from the walls—strike the capital itself.”

sentences.zh: 得長安，黃白城自服。

translations.literal: “Take Chang’an and Huangbai must yield on its own.”
translations.idiomatic: “Break Chang’an and Huangbai collapses without a blow.”

sentences.zh: 願大王以重眾守此，染請輕騎襲之。

translations.literal: “Let the great king pin them with a heavy force here; Ran asks leave to raid with light horse.”
translations.idiomatic: “Hold them here with your main column while I dart in with cavalry.”

sentences.zh: 」曜乃承制加染前鋒大都督、安南大將軍，以精騎五千配之而進。

translations.literal: ” Yao thereupon invested Ran as grand commander of the vanguard and grand general who pacifies the south, assigning him five thousand picked riders for the thrust.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Yao named Zhao Ran commander of the van and general who pacifies the south and gave him five thousand elite horsemen.

sentences.zh: 王師敗于渭陽，將軍王廣死之。

translations.literal: Imperial troops fell at Weiyang; general Wang Guang died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Jin soldiers lost at Weiyang; Wang Guang died on the field.

sentences.zh: 染夜入長安外城，帝奔射雁樓，染焚燒龍尾及諸軍營，殺掠千餘人，旦退屯逍遙園。

translations.literal: Ran slipped into Chang’an’s outer enclosure by night; the emperor fled to the Wild-Goose Archery Tower; Ran burned the Dragon-Tail rampart and several camps, slaughtered and plundered over a thousand souls, then at dawn withdrew to Rambling Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ran infiltrated the outer wall by night, drove Emperor Min onto the Goose-Shooting Loft, torched the Dragon-Tail earthworks and barracks, butchered a thousand people, and by sunrise camped again in Rambling Garden.

sentences.zh: 麹允率眾襲曜，連戰敗之。

translations.literal: Qu Yun led troops against Liu Yao and defeated him in successive clashes.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun counterattacked Liu Yao and handed him a string of defeats.

sentences.zh: 曜入粟邑，遂歸平陽。

translations.literal: Yao withdrew into Suyi, then returned to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao pulled back into Suyi and eventually retreated to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 時流星起於牽牛，入紫微，龍形委蛇，其光照地，落於平陽北十里。

translations.literal: A meteor then streaked from the Ox constellation into Purple Tenuity, writhing like a dragon; its glare lit the ground where it fell ten li north of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: A fireball crawled from the Ox asterism into the Purple Palace like a dragon and slammed down ten li north of Pingyang in blinding light.

sentences.zh: 視之，則有肉長三十步，廣二十七步，臭聞於平陽，肉旁常有哭聲，晝夜不止。

translations.literal: Inspectors found flesh thirty paces long and twenty-seven wide; the stench reached Pingyang; wailing sounded beside it day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Men found a slab of flesh nine metres long, groaning audibly; the stench rolled into Pingyang without pause.

sentences.zh: 聰甚惡之，延公卿已下問曰：「朕之不德，致有斯異，其各極言，勿有所諱。

translations.literal: Cong loathed the omen and summoned the high ministers: “Our lack of virtue has produced this strangeness—speak plainly and hide nothing.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong, revolted, demanded blunt counsel: “My sins have summoned this horror—confess what you see.”

sentences.zh: 」陳元達及博士張師等進對曰：「星變之異，其禍行及，臣恐後庭有三后之事，亡國喪家，靡不由此，願陛下慎之。

translations.literal: ” Chen Yuanda and Erudite Zhang Shi replied: “Heaven’s omens strike swiftly; we fear strife among three empresses in the rear palace—lost kingdoms stem from such chaos; beware.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Chen Yuanda and Zhang Shi answered: “Signs this grim strike quickly—we dread rivalry among three queen-consorts; dynasties fall from such storms—be warned.”

sentences.zh: 」聰曰：「此陰陽之理，何關人事！

translations.literal: ” Cong said: “That is yin-yang mechanics—what has it to do with human affairs!”
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Cong snapped: “Cosmic clutter—leave mankind out of it!”

sentences.zh: 」既而劉氏產一蛇一猛獸，各害人而走，尋之不得，頃之，見在隕肉之旁。

translations.literal: ” Soon Lady Liu bore a snake and a savage beast; both killed people and vanished; shortly they reappeared beside the fallen flesh.
translations.idiomatic: ” Soon Empress Liu delivered a serpent and a monstrous cub that mauled servants and vanished, only to reappear beside the meteoric flesh.

sentences.zh: 俄而劉氏死，乃失此肉，哭聲亦止。

translations.literal: Moments later Lady Liu died; the flesh vanished and the keening ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress died the flesh dissolved and the crying stopped.

sentences.zh: 自是後宮亂寵，進禦無序矣。

translations.literal: Afterward favour in the harem ran riot and scheduling of the imperial bed fell into chaos.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the inner palace dissolved into jealous chaos and the roster of night companions collapsed into disorder.

sentences.zh: 聰以劉易為太尉。

translations.literal: Cong appointed Liu Yi grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong named Liu Yi commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 初置相國，官上公，有殊勳德者死乃贈之。

translations.literal: He first created the office of chief minister, ranking above dukes, awarded posthumously only to men of extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: He invented the post of minister paramount—above ordinary dukes—to be granted only after death to men of legendary service.

sentences.zh: 於是大定百官，置太師、丞相，自大司馬以上七公，位皆上公，綠綟綬，遠遊冠。

translations.literal: He then reorganised the bureaucracy: grand preceptor and chancellor joined six posts from grand marshal upward as the Seven Supremes, each wearing green ribbons and “far-roaming” caps.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the ministries: grand tutor, chancellor, and five posts from grand marshal upward formed the Seven Supremes in green ribbons and travelling crowns.

sentences.zh: 置輔漢，都護，中軍，上軍，輔軍，鎮、衛京，前、後、左、右、上、下軍，輔國，冠軍，龍驤，武牙大將軍，營各配兵二千，皆以諸子為之。

translations.literal: He founded Assist-Han, chief protector, central, upper, auxiliary, garrison, capital-guard, front, rear, left, right, upper, lower, bulwark-of-state, champion, dragon-soaring, and martial-fang grand commands—two thousand troops each—and handed every camp to one of his sons.
translations.idiomatic: New banners—Assist Han, chief protector, central host, wings and rear guards, capital sentinels, dragon-soaring hosts—each held two thousand soldiers and went to a princeling.

sentences.zh: 置左右司隸，各領戶二十餘萬，萬戶置一內史，凡內史四十三。

translations.literal: Left and right metropolitan inspectors each governed more than two hundred thousand households; every ten thousand households gained an interior scribe—forty-three in all.
translations.idiomatic: Twin metropolitan inspectors ruled forty-three interior scribes over two hundred thousand households apiece.

sentences.zh: 單于左右輔，各主六夷十萬落，萬落置一都尉。

translations.literal: Chanyu’s left and right aides each commanded a hundred thousand barbarian settlements; every ten thousand settlements had a commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu’s adjutants governed hundred-thousand tribal cantons grouped under commandants of ten thousand tents.

sentences.zh: 省吏部，置左右選曹尚書。

translations.literal: He abolished the Ministry of Personnel and split appointments between left and right selection bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel ministry vanished; twin bureaus of appointment took its place.

sentences.zh: 自司隸以下六官，皆位次僕射。

translations.literal: From metropolitan inspectors downward six ministries ranked immediately below the vice-directorship.
translations.idiomatic: Six ministries beneath the inspectors stood just under the palace vice-directors.

sentences.zh: 置御史大夫及州牧，位皆亞公。

translations.literal: He restored imperial counsellor and provincial shepherd posts, each one notch below duke.
translations.idiomatic: He revived grand counsellor and provincial governors as near-dukes.

sentences.zh: 以其子粲為丞相、領大將軍、錄尚書事，進封晉王，食五都。

translations.literal: His son Liu Can became chancellor, concurrently grand general and recorder of affairs, promoted Prince of Jin with revenue from five metropolitan districts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can took chancellor’s seals, retained grand general and recorder titles, rose as Prince of Jin fed by five capital prefectures.

sentences.zh: 劉延年錄尚書六條事，劉景為太師，王育為太傅，任顗為太保，馬景為大司徒，朱紀為大司空，劉曜為大司馬。

translations.literal: Liu Yannian recorded the Six Articles; Liu Jing became grand preceptor; Wang Yu grand tutor; Ren Yi grand guardian; Ma Jing grand steward; Zhu Ji minister of works; Liu Yao grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yannian oversaw the Six Articles; Liu Jing, Wang Yu, Ren Yi, Ma Jing, Zhu Ji, and Liu Yao filled the elder statesmen’s chairs.

sentences.zh: 曜復次渭汭，趙染次新豐。

translations.literal: Liu Yao camped again at the bend of the Wei; Zhao Ran pitched at Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao bridged the Wei narrows while Zhao Ran dug in at Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 索綝自長安東討染，染狃於累捷，有輕綝之色。

translations.literal: Suo Lin marched east from Chang’an against Ran, who, flushed with easy victories, sneered at Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Lin rode east from Chang’an; Zhao Ran, drunk on winning streaks, mocked him.

sentences.zh: 長史魯徽曰：「今司馬鄴君臣自以逼僭王畿，雄劣不同，必致死距我，將軍宜整陣案兵以擊之，弗可輕也。

translations.literal: Chief clerk Lu Hui warned: “Sima Ye’s court thinks itself cornered inside the royal domain; strength differs— they will fight to the death. Marshal your ranks and strike deliberately—do not treat them lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hui urged caution: “Trapped inside the imperial periphery, Sima Ye’s court will fight like rats in a sack—hold your line and strike measured blows.”

sentences.zh: 困獸猶鬥，況于國乎！

translations.literal: Even a beast at bay still bites—how much more a state!”
translations.idiomatic: Even cornered vermin bite—what of a kingdom!”

sentences.zh: 」染曰：「以司馬模之強，吾取之如拉朽。

translations.literal: ” Ran said: “Against Sima Mo’s strength I pulled him down like rotten timber.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhao Ran sneered: “I shattered Sima Mo like dry rot.”

sentences.zh: 索綝小豎，豈能汙吾馬蹄刀刃邪！

translations.literal: “Suo Lin is a mere boy—can he foul my hooves or blade?”
translations.idiomatic: “Suo Lin is a strippling—hardly worth muddying my sword.”

sentences.zh: 要擒之而後食。

translations.literal: “I shall seize him and dine afterward.”
translations.idiomatic: “I will cage him before supper.”

sentences.zh: 」晨率精騎數百，馳出逆之，戰於城西，敗績而歸，悔曰：「吾不用魯徽之言，以至於此，何面見之！

translations.literal: ” At dawn he led several hundred picked riders to challenge Lin west of the city, suffered defeat, and returning groaned: “I ignored Lu Hui—what face have I left?”
translations.idiomatic: ” At dawn he galloped west with picked riders, crashed against Suo Lin, fled bleeding, and moaned, “Lu Hui warned me—how do I face him now?”

sentences.zh: 」於是斬徽。

translations.literal: ” Then he executed Lu Hui.
translations.idiomatic: ” So he beheaded Lu Hui instead.

sentences.zh: 徽臨刑謂染曰：「將軍愎諫違謀，戇而取敗，而復忌前害勝，誅戮忠良，以逞愚忿，亦何顏面瞬息世間哉！

translations.literal: Facing execution Hui told Ran: “You spurn counsel, invite defeat, yet envy your betters and butcher loyalty to soothe stupidity—what cheek remains to walk the sunlit world!
translations.idiomatic: At the block Lu Hui spat: “You refused wisdom, lost the field, then slew the faithful to salve your pride—have you no shame under Heaven!”

sentences.zh: 袁紹為之于前，將軍踵之于後，覆亡敗喪，亦當相尋，所恨不得一見大司馬而死。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao did likewise before you; you follow—ruin will stalk you too; my only regret is dying before I see the grand marshal.”
translations.idiomatic: “Yuan Shao murdered Tian Feng before defeat; you mirror him—ruin follows such men. I only regret missing Liu Yao’s reckoning.”

sentences.zh: 死者無知則已；

translations.literal: “If death ends awareness—so be it;
translations.idiomatic: “If oblivion waits beyond death—farewell;

sentences.zh: 若其有知，下見田豐為徒，要當訴將軍于黃泉，使將軍不得服床枕而死。

translations.literal: if not, below ground I shall join Tian Feng and indict you before the Yellow Springs so you fall without a pillow.”
translations.idiomatic: if not, I shall haunt you beside Tian Feng until you die without a deathbed.”

sentences.zh: 」叱刑者曰：「令吾面東向。

translations.literal: ” He ordered the headsman: “Turn my eyes east.”
translations.idiomatic: ” He told the executioner: “Face me toward the east.”

sentences.zh: 」大司馬曜聞之曰：「蹄涔不容尺鯉，染之謂也。」

translations.literal: ” Grand marshal Liu Yao remarked: “A hoof-print puddle cannot hide a foot-long carp—that is Zhao Ran.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Yao muttered, “A puddle cannot hold a carp—such is Zhao Ran.”

sentences.zh: 曜還師攻郭默於懷城，收其米粟八十萬斛，列三屯以守之。

translations.literal: Yao withdrew his army to storm Guo Mo at Huai fortress, confiscated eight hundred thousand hu of grain, and ringed three camps around the stores.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao doubled back on Huai, seized eight hundred thousand hu from Guo Mo, and threw up three fortified depots.

sentences.zh: 聰遣使謂曜曰：「今長安假息，劉琨遊魂，此國家所尤宜先除也。

translations.literal: Cong sent envoys instructing Yao: “Chang’an still breathes and Liu Kun wanders like a ghost—the state must uproot them first.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong’s messengers told Liu Yao: “Chang’an still gasps and Liu Kun haunts the frontier—finish them before anything else.”

sentences.zh: 郭默小丑，何足以勞公神略，可留征虜將軍貝丘王翼光守之，公其還也。

translations.literal: “Guo Mo is a petty bandit—not worth wasting your stratagem; leave Campaign General Wang Yiguang of Beqiu to pin him while you withdraw.”
translations.idiomatic: “Guo Mo is a nuisance—hardly worth your genius. Leave Wang Yiguang, the campaign general of Beqiu, to bottle him up and come home.”

sentences.zh: 」於是曜歸薄阪。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Liu Yao withdrew to Boban.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Yao broke camp and retired to Boban.

sentences.zh: 俄而徵曜輔政。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Liu Cong recalled Liu Yao to serve as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter Liu Cong summoned Liu Yao back to court to share the government.

sentences.zh: 趙染寇北地，夢魯徽大怒，引弓射之，染驚悸而寤。

translations.literal: Zhao Ran raided Beidi; he dreamed that Lu Hui, furious, bent a bow and shot him—Ran jolted awake in terror.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhao Ran struck Beidi he dreamed Lu Hui drawing a bow against him; he woke drenched in sweat.

sentences.zh: 旦將攻城，中弩而死。

translations.literal: At dawn, as he prepared to storm the walls, a crossbow bolt killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When morning came and he moved to assault the city, a quarrel bolt cut him down.

sentences.zh: 聰以粲為相國，總百揆，省丞相以並相國。

translations.literal: Liu Cong named Liu Can minister of state with authority over every bureau and abolished the separate title of chancellor, folding it into that office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong made Liu Can minister of state with sweeping powers and merged the old chancellorship into the post.

sentences.zh: 平陽地震，烈風拔樹髮屋。

translations.literal: Pingyang shook in an earthquake; gales tore up trees and ripped away roofs.
translations.idiomatic: An earthquake rocked Pingyang while whirlwinds uprooted timber and stripped houses bare.

sentences.zh: 光義人羊充妻產子二頭，其兄竊而食之，三日而死。

translations.literal: In Guangyi a woman named Yang Chong’s wife bore twins fused at the crown; her elder brother stole and ate them and died within three days.
translations.idiomatic: A Guangyi woman delivered two-headed twins; her brother stole and devoured them and was dead three days later.

sentences.zh: 聰以其太廟新成，大赦境內，改年建元。

translations.literal: Because his dynastic temple had just been finished, Liu Cong proclaimed a general amnesty and adopted the reign title Jianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: With the new ancestral shrine complete, Liu Cong declared amnesty and renamed the era Jianyuan.

sentences.zh: 雨血於其東宮延明殿，徹瓦在地者深五寸。

translations.literal: Blood rain drenched the Yanming Hall of the eastern palace; fallen tiles lay five cun deep.
translations.idiomatic: Red rain splashed the Yanming Hall until smashed tiles piled finger-deep on the pavement.

sentences.zh: 劉乂惡之，以訪其太師盧志、太傅崔瑋、太保許遐。

translations.literal: Prince Liu Yi took fright and consulted his tutors Lu Zhi, Cui Wei, and Xu Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Liu Yi sought counsel from Lu Zhi, Cui Wei, and Xu Xia.

sentences.zh: 志等曰：「主上往以殿下為太弟者，蓋以安眾望也，志在晉王久矣，王公已下莫不希旨歸之。

translations.literal: They replied: “The sovereign once named you heir apparent only to calm public opinion; his heart has long settled on Prince Jin, and every noble echoes that wish.”
translations.idiomatic: They answered: “The throne made you heir apparent merely to quiet the court—the king’s eye has rested on Prince Jin for years, and every minister trims his sails to match.”

sentences.zh: 相國之位，自魏武已來，非復人臣之官，主上本發明詔，置之為贈官，今忽以晉王居之，羽儀威尊逾于東宮，萬機之事無不由之，置太宰、大將軍及諸王之營以為羽翼，此事勢去矣，殿下不得立明也。

translations.literal: Since Cao Cao’s day the minister of state has ceased to be a mere minister’s post; Your Majesty once issued an edict reserving it for posthumous honour—yet now Prince Jin occupies it with retinue grander than the heir’s. Every state decision passes through him, while grand tutors, marshals, and princely camps prop him up—the tide has turned; you cannot inherit.”
translations.idiomatic: “Ever since Wei times ‘minister of state’ has meant more than a servant’s title—your brother himself called it a mortuary honour—yet Prince Jin now fills it with panoply surpassing the crown prince’s. Policy flows through his hands while marshals and younger princes shore him up; the succession is lost.”

sentences.zh: 然非止不得立而已，不測之危厄在於旦夕，宜早為之所。

translations.literal: Not only will you fail to succeed—disaster may strike between dawn and dusk; you must act now.
translations.idiomatic: You may never mount the throne at all—peril could strike within hours—move before it does.

sentences.zh: 四衛精兵不減五千，余營諸王皆年齒尚幼，可奪而取之。

translations.literal: The palace guard still fields five thousand veterans; the other princely camps are boys—you can seize them.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand crack household troops remain at hand, and the other princely encampments are led by children—you can disarm them.

sentences.zh: 相國輕佻，正可煩一刺客耳。

translations.literal: The minister of state is reckless—a lone dagger-man could finish him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can is careless; one assassin would suffice.

sentences.zh: 大將軍無日不出，其營可襲而得也。

translations.literal: The grand marshal leaves camp daily—you could storm his headquarters empty-handed.
translations.idiomatic: The grand marshal rides out every morning—you could take his barracks by surprise.

sentences.zh: 殿下但當有意，二萬精兵立便可得，鼓行向雲龍門，宿衛之士孰不倒戈奉迎，大司馬不慮為異也。

translations.literal: Summon twenty thousand picked troops, beat drums to the Cloud-Dragon Gate, and the household guards will drop their halberds to greet you; the grand marshal will not dare resist.”
translations.idiomatic: Raise twenty thousand elites, march on the Cloud-Dragon Gate, and the household corps will welcome you with lowered weapons; Liu Yao will not stand in your way.”

sentences.zh: 」乂弗從，乃止。

translations.literal: Yi refused; the plot died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi would not move, and the conspiracy collapsed.

sentences.zh: 聰如中護軍靳准第，納其二女為左右貴嬪，大曰月光，小曰月華，皆國色也。

translations.literal: Liu Cong visited Director Jin Zhun’s mansion and took his daughters as senior concubines left and right—the elder Moonlight, the younger Moon Splendour—both famed beauties.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong called at Jin Zhun’s house and carried off his daughters as twin favourites, Moonlight and Moon Splendour, each a paragon of loveliness.

sentences.zh: 數月，立月光為皇后。

translations.literal: Within months he elevated Moonlight to empress.
translations.idiomatic: Months later Moonlight wore the empress’s crown.

sentences.zh: 東宮舍人荀裕告盧志等勸乂謀反，乂不從之狀。
