translations.literal: Palace secretary Xun Yu reported how Lu Zhi had urged Liu Yi to rebel and how Yi rejected them.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu of the heir’s household denounced Lu Zhi’s sedition and swore Liu Yi had refused.

sentences.zh: 聰於是收志、瑋、遐於詔獄，假以他事殺之。

translations.literal: Liu Cong jailed Lu Zhi, Cui Wei, and Xu Xia on trumped-up charges and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong threw the three advisers into the imperial prison and killed them under false pretences.

sentences.zh: 使冠威卜抽監守東宮，禁乂朝賀。

translations.literal: He ordered Bu Chou to seal the heir’s compound and barred Liu Yi from court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: He set Bu Chou to cordon the eastern palace and forbade Liu Yi the New Year levee.

sentences.zh: 乂憂懼不知所為，乃上表自陳，乞為黔首，並免諸子之封，褒美晉王粲宜登儲副，抽又抑而弗通。

translations.literal: Yi, frantic, memorialised begging to be reduced to commoner status, stripped his sons of titles, and praised Prince Jin as rightful heir—yet Bu Chou suppressed the petition.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi pleaded in writing to become a commoner, surrender his sons’ fiefs, and hail Liu Can as successor; Bu Chou buried the memorial.

sentences.zh: 其青州刺史曹嶷攻汶陽關、公丘，陷之，害齊郡太守徐浮，執建威劉宣，齊魯之間郡縣壘壁降者四十餘所。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Qingzhou inspector Cao Yi stormed Wenyang Pass and Gongqiu, slew Qi prefect Xu Fu, captured Liu Xuan, and forced forty strongholds between Qi and Lu to yield.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yi of Qingzhou ripped through Wenyang and Gongqiu, killed Xu Fu of Qi, bagged Liu Xuan, and compelled forty forts from Qi to Lu to submit.

sentences.zh: 嶷遂略地，西下祝阿、平陰，眾十餘萬，臨河置戍，而歸於臨淄。

translations.literal: Yi swept west through Zhu’e and Pingyin with more than a hundred thousand men, planted river pickets, and returned to Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: He swept west through Zhu’e and Pingyin at the head of a hundred thousand warriors, threw bridgeheads along the Yellow River, and pulled back to Linzi.

sentences.zh: 嶷於是遂雄據全齊之志。

translations.literal: From this he meant to dominate all Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He now aimed to master the whole Shandong plain.

sentences.zh: 石勒以嶷之懷二也，請討之。

translations.literal: Shi Le, suspecting Yi’s double loyalty, asked leave to destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le, scenting treason, begged for a campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 聰又憚勒之並齊，乃寢而弗許。

translations.literal: Liu Cong feared Shi Le would swallow Qi whole and shelved the request.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong dreaded letting Shi Le annex Qi and left the plea unanswered.

sentences.zh: 劉曜濟自盟津，將攻河南，將軍魏該奔於一泉塢。

translations.literal: Liu Yao crossed at Meng Ford to strike Henan; General Wei Gai fled into Yiquan stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao forded the Meng crossing toward Henan while Wei Gai bolted into the Yiquan redoubt.

sentences.zh: 曜進攻李矩于滎陽，矩遣將軍李平師于成皋，曜覆而滅之。

translations.literal: Yao assaulted Li Ju at Xingyang; Ju sent Li Ping to Chenggao, and Yao ambushed and annihilated him.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Li Ju at Xingyang, crushed Li Ping’s relief column at Chenggao in an ambush, and scattered the Jin army.

sentences.zh: 矩恐，送質請降。

translations.literal: Ju panicked, sent hostages, and sued for surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju panicked, handed over hostages, and capitulated.

sentences.zh: 時聰以其皇后靳氏為上皇后，立貴妃劉氏為左皇后，右貴嬪靳氏為右皇后。

translations.literal: Liu Cong now styled Empress Jin “supreme empress,” promoted Consort Liu to empress of the left, and Jin’s cousin on the right to empress of the right.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong crowned three queens—Lady Jin as paramount consort, Lady Liu as senior left, another Lady Jin as senior right.

sentences.zh: 左司隸陳元達以三后之立也，極諫，聰不納，乃以元達為右光祿大夫，外示優賢，內實奪其權也。

translations.literal: Left metropolitan inspector Chen Yuanda protested vehemently; Liu Cong ignored him but named him grandee of the Household Rapid on the right—a public honour that secretly stripped his voice.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuanda thundered against the triple enthronement; Liu Cong answered by promoting him to a powerless grandee of the Household Rapid on the right.

sentences.zh: 於是太尉范隆、大司馬劉丹、大司空呼延晏、尚書令王鑒等皆抗表遜位，以讓元達。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Fan Long, Grand Marshal Liu Dan, Minister Huyan Yan, and Director Wang Jian then offered their seals to yield place to Yuanda.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Long, Liu Dan, Huyan Yan, and Wang Jian resigned en masse to force Yuanda’s reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 聰乃以元達為御史大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Liu Cong made Yuanda imperial counsellor with ceremonial rank matching the three dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong restored him as chief censor with honours equal to the three elder ministers.

sentences.zh: 劉曜寇長安，頻為王師所敗。

translations.literal: Liu Yao raided Chang’an but Jin armies beat him repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao struck Chang’an again and again yet Jin drove him back each time.

sentences.zh: 曜曰：「彼猶強盛，弗可圖矣。

translations.literal: Yao said: “They remain too strong—there is nothing to gain.”
translations.idiomatic: “They are still formidable,” Liu Yao admitted; “there is no opening.”

sentences.zh: 」引師而歸。

translations.literal: He withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: He broke off and marched home.

sentences.zh: 聰宮中鬼夜哭，三日而聲向右司隸寺，乃止。

translations.literal: Ghosts wailed nightly in Liu Cong’s palace for three nights until the sound drifted toward the right metropolitan office and ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits keened through Liu Cong’s halls for three nights, then drifted toward the western inspectorate and fell silent.

sentences.zh: 其上皇后靳氏有淫穢之行，陳元達奏之。

translations.literal: Supreme Empress Jin’s adultery reached Chen Yuanda’s memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuanda impeached the paramount consort for debauchery.

sentences.zh: 聰廢靳，靳慚恚自殺。

translations.literal: Liu Cong deposed her; she killed herself in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong cast her aside; she took her own life in humiliation.

sentences.zh: 靳有殊寵，聰迫于元達之勢，故廢之。

translations.literal: She had enjoyed unrivalled favour; Liu Cong acted only because Yuanda’s pressure left no choice.
translations.idiomatic: Once his favourite, she fell because Yuanda left him no face-saving alternative.

sentences.zh: 既而追念其姿色，深仇元達。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he missed her beauty and nursed a bitter grudge against Yuanda.
translations.idiomatic: Soon nostalgia for her beauty curdled into hatred for Yuanda.

sentences.zh: 劉曜進師上黨，將攻陽曲，聰遣使謂曜曰：「長安擅命，國家之深恥也。

translations.literal: Liu Yao pushed into Shangdang intending to take Yangqu; Liu Cong sent word: “Chang’an’s defiance remains our deepest humiliation.”
translations.idiomatic: As Liu Yao advanced on Yangqu from Shangdang, Liu Cong’s messengers warned him: “Chang’an’s stubbornness shames the dynasty.”

sentences.zh: 公宜以長安為先，陽曲一委驃騎。

translations.literal: “Make Chang’an your first concern; leave Yangqu to the cavalry marshal.”
translations.idiomatic: “Strike Chang’an first—hand Yangqu to the cavalry commander.”

sentences.zh: 天時人事，其應至矣，公其亟還。

translations.literal: “Heaven and men alike demand action—return at once.”
translations.idiomatic: “Heaven and earth cry for vengeance—return immediately.”

sentences.zh: 」曜回滅郭邁，朝於聰，遂如蒲阪。

translations.literal: ” Liu Yao wheeled about, destroyed Guo Mai, audience Liu Cong, then moved to Puban.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Yao smashed Guo Mai on the way back, paid court at Pingyang, and encamped at Puban.

sentences.zh: 平陽地震，雨血於東宮，廣袤頃餘。

translations.literal: Pingyang quaked again; blood rain soaked the eastern palace across more than a qing.
translations.idiomatic: Another tremor shook Pingyang while red rain drenched a whole qing of the heir’s compound.

sentences.zh: 劉曜又進軍，屯於粟邑。

translations.literal: Liu Yao advanced once more and camped at Suyi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao pushed forward again and dug in at Suyi.

sentences.zh: 麹允饑甚，去黃白而軍于靈武。

translations.literal: Starving, Qu Yun abandoned Huangbai for Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun, half dead of hunger, quit Huangbai for Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 曜進攻上郡，太守張禹與馮翊太守梁肅奔於允吾。

translations.literal: Yao struck Shang commandery; prefects Zhang Yu and Liang Su of Fengyi fled to Yunwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao hit Shang commandery, Zhang Yu and Liang Su bolted for Yunwu.

sentences.zh: 於是關右翕然，所在應曜。

translations.literal: The Guanzhong west therefore rallied to Liu Yao.
translations.idiomatic: All western Guanzhong then hailed Liu Yao’s banners.

sentences.zh: 曜進據黃阜。

translations.literal: Yao seized Huangfu.
translations.idiomatic: He occupied the Huangfu heights.

sentences.zh: 聰武庫陷入地一丈五尺。

translations.literal: Liu Cong’s arsenal sank fifteen chi into the earth.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial armoury yard collapsed fifteen chi into the ground.

sentences.zh: 時聰中常侍王沈、宣懷、俞容，中宮僕射郭猗，中黃門陵修等皆寵倖用事。

translations.literal: Attendants Wang Shen, Xuan Huai, Yu Rong, overseer Guo Yi, and eunuch Ling Xiu curried favour and ran the government.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen, Xuan Huai, Yu Rong, Guo Yi, and Ling Xiu traded on intimacy and seized the levers of power.

sentences.zh: 聰游宴後宮，或百日不出，群臣皆因沈等言事，多不呈聰，率以其意愛憎而決之，故或有勳舊功臣而弗見敘錄，奸佞小人數日而便至二千石者。

translations.literal: Liu Cong banqueted in the harem for stretches of a hundred days; ministers relayed business only through these favourites, seldom reaching the emperor—promotions followed private whims, so meritorious elders languished unrecorded while rogues vaulted to two-thousand-shi salaries overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong vanished into the inner palaces for months; petitions flowed through his favourites, honours tracked private spite, veterans went unrewarded while sycophants leapt to top salaries in days.

sentences.zh: 軍旅無歲不興，而將士無錢帛之賞，後宮之家賜齎及於僮僕，動至數千萬。

translations.literal: Campaigns raged every year yet troops saw no cash rewards; consorts’ kin pocketed millions down to household slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Armies marched yearly without pay while imperial in-laws scattered millions even on servants.

sentences.zh: 沈等車服宅宇皆逾于諸王，子弟、中表布衣為內史令長者三十餘人，皆奢僭貪殘，賊害良善。

translations.literal: The favourites outshone princes in carriages and mansions; thirty-odd kinsmen held county posts though barely commoners—luxurious, cruel predators.
translations.idiomatic: They outsized true princes in coaches and villas; thirty cousins ruled counties despite mean birth—every one tyrannical and corrupt.

sentences.zh: 靳准合宗內外諂以事之。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun’s entire clan flattered them inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun’s clan crawled before them at court and in camp.

sentences.zh: 郭猗有憾于劉乂，謂劉粲曰：「太弟于主上之世猶懷不逞之志，此則殿下父子之深仇，四海蒼生之重怨也。

translations.literal: Guo Yi hated Liu Yi and told Liu Can: “Your uncle still nurses treason—your father’s mortal foe and the empire’s scourge.”
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi whispered to Liu Can: “The imperial younger brother still plots sedition—your father’s bitter enemy and the world’s bane.”

sentences.zh: 而主上過垂寬仁，猶不替二尊之位，一旦有風塵之變，臣竊為殿下寒心。

translations.literal: “Yet His Majesty stays merciful and leaves both elders in place—should turmoil erupt I tremble for you.”
translations.idiomatic: “Yet the emperor’s mercy keeps him in post—if crisis strikes you will be first to fall.”

sentences.zh: 且殿下高祖之世孫，主上之嫡統，凡在含齒，孰不系仰。

translations.literal: “You are the founding emperor’s great-grandson and sole legitimate heir—every toothed creature looks to you.”
translations.idiomatic: “You are Guangwen’s lineal descendant—the realm pins its hope on you alone.”

sentences.zh: 萬機事大，何可與人！

translations.literal: “The myriad threads of rule—how can you share them?”
translations.idiomatic: “The machinery of state is not a toy to share.”

sentences.zh: 臣昨聞太弟與大將軍相見，極有言矣，若事成，許以主上為在太上皇，大將軍為皇太子。

translations.literal: “Yesterday I heard him bargain with the grand marshal: succeed and your father becomes retired emperor while the marshal becomes heir.”
translations.idiomatic: “Yesterday he promised the grand marshal: succeed and Father becomes a retired sovereign while the marshal inherits.”

sentences.zh: 乂又許衛軍為大單于，二王已許之矣。

translations.literal: “He likewise pledged the guard marshal the title of great Chanyu—both princes agreed.”
translations.idiomatic: “He offered the guard marshal the great Chanyu’s throne—both military princes accepted.”

sentences.zh: 二王居不疑之地，並握重兵，以此舉事，事何不成！

translations.literal: “They hold unquestioned commands and heavy armies—how can such a coup fail?”
translations.idiomatic: “They command unquestioned hosts—what could stop them?”

sentences.zh: 臣謂二王茲舉，禽獸之不若也。

translations.literal: “In my eyes they behave worse than beasts.”
translations.idiomatic: “They sink below beasts.”

sentences.zh: 背父親人，人豈親之！

translations.literal: “Betray fathers and kin—who will call them kin?”
translations.idiomatic: “Men who sell father and brother earn no loyalty.”

sentences.zh: 今又苟貪其一切之力耳，事成之後，主上豈有全理！

translations.literal: “They crave your strength for the moment; afterward do you think Father survives?”
translations.idiomatic: “They borrow your steel today—do you imagine Father lives tomorrow?”

sentences.zh: 殿下兄弟故在忘言，東宮、相國、單于在武陵兄弟，何肯與人！

translations.literal: “Your brothers need no persuasion—the heir, minister of state, and Chanyu at Wuling will never yield power willingly.”
translations.idiomatic: “Your brothers at Wuling—the heir, the minister of state, the Chanyu—will never surrender their swords.”

sentences.zh: 許以三月上巳因宴作難，事淹變生，宜早為之所。

translations.literal: “They plot for the third-month festival banquet; delay breeds betrayal—strike first.”
translations.idiomatic: “They chose the spring festival banquet for the coup—move before plans ripen.”

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳》曰：'蔓草猶不可除，況君之寵弟乎！

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary says: “Rank weeds cannot be uprooted—how much less a sovereign’s favoured brother!”
translations.idiomatic: As the Zuo says: “Weeds left to spread cannot be torn out—far less a king’s pampered brother.”

sentences.zh: '臣屢啟主上，主上性敦友于，謂臣言不實。

translations.literal: “I have warned His Majesty; his fond brotherly heart dismisses me.”
translations.idiomatic: “I have warned the throne; brotherly fondness blinds him.”

sentences.zh: 刑臣刀鋸之余，而蒙主上、殿下成造之恩，故不慮逆鱗之誅，每所聞必言，冀垂採納。

translations.literal: “I am a mutilated leftover yet owe you both creation—therefore I risk the dragon scales and speak.”
translations.idiomatic: “I am a castrated survivor yet owe you both everything—so I brave imperial wrath.”

sentences.zh: 臣當入言之。

translations.literal: “I shall repeat this above.”
translations.idiomatic: “I will speak upstairs myself.”

sentences.zh: 願殿下不泄，密表其狀也。

translations.literal: “Guard the secret—memorialise beneath seal.”
translations.idiomatic: “Tell no one—petition him under seal.”

sentences.zh: 若不信臣言，可呼大將軍從事中郎王皮、衛軍司馬劉惇，假之恩顧，通其歸善之路以問之，必可知也。

translations.literal: “If you doubt me, summon Wang Pi and Liu Dun, treat them kindly, open a path to confession—you will learn the truth.”
translations.idiomatic: “Summon Wang Pi and Liu Dun, win them with kindness, and they will confess.”

sentences.zh: 」粲深然之。

translations.literal: Liu Can believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can swallowed every word.

sentences.zh: 猗密謂皮、惇曰：「二王逆狀，主、相已具知之矣，卿同之乎？

translations.literal: Guo Yi privately told Wang Pi and Liu Dun: “Lord and minister already know the two princes’ treason—do you?”
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi cornered Wang Pi and Liu Dun: “Court and camp already know the princes plot—do you?”

sentences.zh: 」二人驚曰？

translations.literal: They started in alarm:
translations.idiomatic: They blurted:

sentences.zh: ：「無之。

translations.literal: “Nothing of the sort.”
translations.idiomatic: “Nothing like that!”

sentences.zh: 」猗曰：「此事必無疑，吾憐卿親舊並見族耳。

translations.literal: Yi said: “No doubt remains—I pity you both facing clan execution.”
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi said: “Then you are doomed with your kin.”

sentences.zh: 」於是歔欷流涕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sobbed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He broke into theatrical tears.

sentences.zh: 皮、惇大懼，叩頭求哀。

translations.literal: Pi and Dun were terrified and knocked their heads begging mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi and Liu Dun fell kowtowing for mercy.

sentences.zh: 猗曰：「吾為卿作計，卿能用不？

translations.literal: Yi said: “I will devise a plan—will you obey?”
translations.idiomatic: “I can save you—will you listen?”

sentences.zh: 」二人皆曰：「謹奉大人之教。

translations.literal: Both said: “We respectfully receive the great man’s teaching.”
translations.idiomatic: “Command us,” they sobbed.

sentences.zh: 」猗曰：「相國必問卿，卿但云有之。

translations.literal: Yi said: “When the minister of state questions you, simply answer yes.”
translations.idiomatic: “When Liu Can asks, confess.”

sentences.zh: 若責卿何不先啟，卿即答云：'臣誠負死罪，然仰惟主上聖性寬慈，殿下篤于骨肉，恐言成詿偽故也。

translations.literal: If he asks why you never reported, answer: “Your servant deserves death—yet His Majesty is merciful and Your Highness loves kin; I feared false accusation.”
translations.idiomatic: If pressed why they stayed silent: “We deserve death—yet the emperor is gentle and you honour kin—so we feared crying wolf.”

sentences.zh: '」皮、惇許諾。

translations.literal: Pi and Dun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: They swore compliance.

sentences.zh: 粲俄而召問二人，至不同時，而辭若畫一，粲以為信然。

translations.literal: Can soon summoned them separately; their stories matched like one brushstroke—Can trusted them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can questioned them apart; identical confessions convinced him.

sentences.zh: 初，靳准從妹為乂孺子，淫于侍人，乂怒殺之，而屢以嘲准。

translations.literal: Earlier Jin Zhun’s cousin had been Liu Yi’s child concubine; she lay with a servant—Yi killed her and mocked Zhun ever after.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun’s cousin served Liu Yi as concubine until he executed her for bedding a page—then mocked Zhun mercilessly.

sentences.zh: 准深慚恚，說粲曰：「東宮萬機之副，殿下宜自居之，以領相國，使天下知早有所系望也。

translations.literal: Zhun, burning with shame, urged Can: “The eastern palace steers policy—you should seize it and head the ministry so the realm knows where to look.”
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated, Jin Zhun urged Liu Can to seize the heir’s administration and lead the ministry himself.

sentences.zh: 」至是，准又說粲曰：「昔孝成距子政之言，使王氏卒成篡逆，可乎？

translations.literal: Later Zhun added: “Emperor Cheng spurned Liu Xiang’s counsel and let the Wang usurp—would you repeat that?”
translations.idiomatic: Later he added: “Emperor Cheng ignored Liu Xiang and handed Jin to Wang Mang—will you copy him?”

sentences.zh: 」粲曰：「何可之有！

translations.literal: Can said: “How could that be permissible!”
translations.idiomatic: “Never,” Liu Can snapped.

sentences.zh: 」准曰：「然，誠如聖旨。

translations.literal: Zhun said: “Precisely—as Your Highness decrees.”
translations.idiomatic: “Exactly as you say,” Jin Zhun murmured.

sentences.zh: 下官亟欲有所言矣，但以德非更生，親非皇宗，恐忠言暫出，霜威已及，故不敢耳。

translations.literal: “This official burns to speak—yet I lack Liu Xiang’s virtue or imperial blood; one loyal word might summon execution.”
translations.idiomatic: “I ache to counsel you—yet I am neither Liu Xiang nor royal kin—truth might cost my head.”

sentences.zh: 」粲曰：「君但言之。

translations.literal: Can said: “Speak freely.”
translations.idiomatic: “Out with it.”

sentences.zh: 」准曰：「聞風塵之言，謂大將軍、衛將軍及左右輔皆謀奉太弟，克季春構變，殿下宜為之備。

translations.literal: Zhun said: “Rumour says the grand marshal, guard marshal, and Chanyu’s deputies mean to enthrone the imperial younger brother this spring—you must prepare.”
translations.idiomatic: “Whispers name the marshals and Chanyu aides backing Liu Yi for a coup late this spring—arm yourself.”

sentences.zh: 不然，恐有商臣之禍。

translations.literal: Otherwise you invite the tragedy of Prince Shangchen.
translations.idiomatic: Refuse and you risk another prince who murders his father to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 」粲曰：「為之奈何？

translations.literal: ” Liu Can asked: “Then what must I do?”
translations.idiomatic: ” “What is your counsel?” Liu Can replied.

sentences.zh: 」准曰：「主上愛信于太弟，恐卒聞未必信也。

translations.literal: ” Jin Zhun said: “His Majesty dotes on the imperial younger brother—shocking news may not convince him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Jin Zhun answered: “The emperor trusts Liu Yi too deeply—a blunt accusation may fail.”

sentences.zh: 如下官愚意，宜緩東宮之禁固，勿絕太弟賓客，使輕薄之徒得與交遊。

translations.literal: In my humble view loosen the cordon around the eastern palace and let his visitors come and go so shallow men can mingle with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ease the heir’s house arrest and admit guests again so riffraff may flock to him.

sentences.zh: 太弟既素好待士，必不思防此嫌，輕薄小人不能無逆意以勸太弟之心。

translations.literal: He loves scholars and will never suspect a trap; petty flatterers will surely whisper rebellion into his ear.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi loves hosting gentlemen and will drop his guard; hangers-on will bait him toward treason.

sentences.zh: 小人有始無終，不能如貫高之流也。

translations.literal: Such men lack staying power—they are no Guan Gaos.
translations.idiomatic: They are no Guan Gao—they burn bright, then bolt.

sentences.zh: 然後下官為殿下露表其罪，殿下與太宰拘太弟所與交通者考問之，窮其事原，主上必以無將之罪罪之。

translations.literal: Then I shall memorialise his guilt while you and the grand tutor seize everyone he meets and wring confessions until the emperor condemns him for abetting revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Next I expose him on paper; you and the grand tutor arrest his circle and torture the truth free—the sovereign must convict him for “acting without orders.”

sentences.zh: 不然，今朝望多歸太弟，主上一旦晏駕，恐殿下不得立矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise the court already cleaves to him; when His Majesty dies you may never inherit.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the elite already backs Liu Yi—once the emperor closes his eyes you lose everything.

sentences.zh: 」於是粲命卜抽引兵去東宮。

translations.literal: ” Liu Can ordered Bu Chou to march the cordon troops away from the eastern palace.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Can pulled Bu Chou’s guards off the heir’s compound.

sentences.zh: 聰自去冬至是，遂不復受朝賀，軍國之事一決於粲，唯發中旨殺生除授，王沈、郭猗等意所欲皆從之。

translations.literal: From that winter onward Liu Cong ceased holding audiences; Liu Can decided every civil and military matter while inner edicts alone handled appointments and executions—whatever Wang Shen or Guo Yi wanted passed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong stopped receiving ministers; Liu Can ruled in his name while eunuch edicts ordered promotions and killings—Wang Shen and Guo Yi dictated policy unchecked.

sentences.zh: 又立市於後庭，與宮人宴戲，或三日不醒。

translations.literal: He opened a marketplace inside the harem and caroused with ladies until he slept three days straight.
translations.idiomatic: He ran a bazaar in the inner palace and drank with concubines until he slept round the clock.

sentences.zh: 聰臨上秋閣，誅其特進綦毋達，太中大夫公師彧，尚書王琰、田歆，少府陳休，左衛卜崇，大司農朱誕等，皆群閹所忌也。

translations.literal: From the Shangqiu Gallery Liu Cong executed his honourary minister Qi Wuda, palace counsellor Gongshi Yu, directors Wang Yan and Tian Xin, chamberlain Chen Xiu, captain Bu Chong, and minister Zhu Dan—every man the eunuchs loathed.
translations.idiomatic: From the autumn tower he butchered Qi Wuda, Gongshi Yu, Wang Yan, Tian Xin, Chen Xiu, Bu Chong, Zhu Dan—each targeted by the palace cabal.

sentences.zh: 侍中卜幹泣諫聰曰：「陛下方隆武宣之化，欲使幽谷無考槃，奈何一旦先誅忠良，將何以垂之於後！

translations.literal: Palace attendant Bu Gan wept: “While Your Majesty spreads the virtue of kings Wu and Xuan you would slaughter loyalty—what lesson does that leave posterity?
translations.idiomatic: Bu Gan sobbed: “You preach the reforms of Han Wudi and Xuandi yet butcher loyal ministers—what precedent is that?”

sentences.zh: 昔秦愛三良而殺之，君子知其不霸。

translations.literal: Even Qin mourned the Three Worthies it murdered—gentlemen knew it could never rule.
translations.idiomatic: Qin cherished the Three Worthies before executing them—wise men knew heaven had withdrawn its mandate.

sentences.zh: 以晉厲之無道，屍三卿之後，猶有不忍之心，陛下如何忽信左右愛憎之言，欲一日屍七卿！

translations.literal: Depraved Jin Li still hesitated before killing three ministers—why trust bedroom gossip and slaughter seven in a morning?
translations.idiomatic: Even wicked King Li of Jin blanched at executing three nobles—will you butcher seven on court whisper?”

sentences.zh: 詔尚在臣間，猶未宣露，乞垂昊天之澤，回雷霆之威。

translations.literal: The edict still rests with me unreleased—pour heaven’s mercy on us and lift this thunderbolt.
translations.idiomatic: The warrant never left my hands—stay your wrath before Heaven recoils.

sentences.zh: 且陛下直欲誅之耳，不露其罪名，何以示四海！

translations.literal: If you mean to kill them, publish their crimes—else how do you face the realm?
translations.idiomatic: If blood must flow, name their offences—else the empire calls this murder.

sentences.zh: 此豈是帝王三訊之法邪！

translations.literal: Is this how an emperor rehearses the three hearings?
translations.idiomatic: Since when does a Son of Heaven skip trial?”

sentences.zh: 」因叩頭流血。

translations.literal: ” He battered his brow until it bled.
translations.idiomatic: ” He dashed his forehead open on the stones.

sentences.zh: 王沈叱幹曰：「卜侍中欲距詔乎？

translations.literal: Wang Shen snarled: “Does Bu Gan defy an edict?”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen barked: “Do you refuse the imperial brush?”

sentences.zh: 」聰拂衣而入，免幹為庶人。

translations.literal: Liu Cong flung his robes aside, stripped Bu Gan to commoner rank, and vanished within.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong swept inside and reduced Bu Gan to common status.

sentences.zh: 太宰劉易及大將軍劉敷、御史大夫陳元達、金紫光祿大夫王延等詣闕諫曰：「臣聞善人者，乾坤之紀，政教之本也。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Liu Yi, Grand General Liu Fu, Censor Chen Yuanda, and Golden-Purple Wang Yan knelt at the gate: “Good men anchor Heaven and Earth—they are the root of rule.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, Liu Fu, Chen Yuanda, and Wang Yan petitioned: “Virtuous ministers are the pivot of state.”

sentences.zh: 邪佞者，宇宙之螟螣，王化之蟊賊也。

translations.literal: Sycophants are vermin gnawing the cosmos—locusts devouring civilisation.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers are cosmic pests chewing through the kingly way.

sentences.zh: 故文王以多士基周，桓靈以群閹亡漢，國之興亡，未有不由此也。

translations.literal: King Wen raised Zhou on wise counsel; Huan and Ling destroyed Han through eunuchs—rise and fall always hinge on this.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou rose on many advisers; the Han fell on a mob of castrates—history repeats without fail.

sentences.zh: 自古明王之世，未嘗有宦者與政，武、元、安、順豈足為故事乎！

translations.literal: No enlightened age lets mutilated men govern—must Emperors Wu, Yuan, An, and Shun be our models?
translations.idiomatic: No sage reign handed steel to eunuchs—why imitate the worst Han disasters?”

sentences.zh: 今王沈等乃處常伯之位，握生死與奪於中，勢傾海內，愛憎任之，矯弄詔旨，欺誣日月，內諂陛下，外佞相國，威權之重，侔於人主矣。

translations.literal: Today Wang Shen sits among chief ministers, clutching life and death, twisting edicts, blotting out sun and moon—flattering you within and Liu Can without until his power rivals the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen holds ministerial seats yet plays creator—his whim replaces law; he fawns on throne and minister alike until his shadow equals yours.

sentences.zh: 王公見之駭目，卿宰望塵下車，銓衡迫之，選舉不復以實，士以屬舉，政以賄成，多樹奸徒，殘毒忠善。

translations.literal: Princes gape in horror; magistrates bow from their carts; appointments sell to factions; bribery decides policy; good men perish while villains multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Nobles stare in dread; prefects grovel in dust; offices go to cliques; justice sells cheap; loyal throats are cut while knaves thrive.

sentences.zh: 知王琰等忠臣，必盡節于陛下，懼其奸萌發露，陷之極刑。

translations.literal: Knowing ministers like Wang Yan would die for you, they framed capital crimes before loyalty could flower.
translations.idiomatic: They struck Wang Yan because his virtue threatened their fraud.

sentences.zh: 陛下不垂三察，猥加誅戮，怨感穹蒼，痛入九泉，四海悲惋，賢愚傷懼。

translations.literal: Without threefold review you butchered them—Heaven groans, ghosts weep, the seas mourn, wise and simple alike tremble.
translations.idiomatic: No deliberation—only blades—and Heaven darkens while the world shudders.

sentences.zh: 沈等皆刀鋸之餘，背恩忘義之類，豈能如士人君子感恩展效，以答乾澤也。

translations.literal: These men are knife-scraped remnants who forgot gratitude—how can they repay royal grace like gentlemen?
translations.idiomatic: They are castrated ingrates—never scholars who honour grace.

sentences.zh: 陛下何故親近之？

translations.literal: Why clasp them to your breast?
translations.idiomatic: Why favour such creatures?”

sentences.zh: 何故貴任之？

translations.literal: Why heap offices on them?
translations.idiomatic: Why bind the realm to their whim?”

sentences.zh: 昔齊桓公任易牙而亂，孝懷委黃皓而滅，此皆覆車於前，殷鑒不遠。

translations.literal: Duke Huan trusted Yiya and fell; Emperor Huai fed Huang Hao and perished—the wheel crushed them before us.
translations.idiomatic: Qi fell on Yiya; Shu drowned in Huang Hao—the wreck lies plain ahead.

sentences.zh: 比年地震日蝕，雨血火災，皆沈等之由。

translations.literal: Earthquakes, eclipses, bloody rain, and infernos these past years all stem from Wang Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Every recent portent traces to Wang Shen’s cabal.

sentences.zh: 願陛下割翦凶醜與政之流，引尚書、御史朝省萬機，相國與公卿五日一入，會議政事，使大臣得極其言，忠臣得逞其意，則眾災自弭，和氣呈祥。

translations.literal: Slash these fiends from power, recall directors and censors to court, require Liu Can and the ministers to convene every fifth day, and disaster will heal itself.
translations.idiomatic: Cut them away, seat real ministers, force weekly councils with Liu Can—harmony returns.

sentences.zh: 今遺晉未殄，巴蜀未賓，石勒潛有跨趙魏之志，曹嶷密有王全齊之心，而復以沈等助亂大政，陛下心腹四支何處無患！

translations.literal: Jin still breathes; Ba and Shu resist; Shi Le eyes Zhao and Wei; Cao Yi schemes for Qi—yet you let Wang Shen poison government—where under your skin is safe?
translations.idiomatic: Enemies ring you while eunuchs rot the core—no limb escapes infection.

sentences.zh: 復誅巫咸，戮扁鵲，臣恐遂成桓侯膏肓之疾，後雖欲療之，其如病何！

translations.literal: Slaying Wu Xian and Bian Que leaves Duke Huan’s tumour uncured—later healers will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: Murder every healer and even Bian Que cannot cure the gangrene you invite.

sentences.zh: 請免沈等官，付有司定罪。

translations.literal: Dismiss them and hand them to the judges.”
translations.idiomatic: Strip their seals for trial.”

sentences.zh: 」聰以表示沈等，笑曰：「是兒等為元達所引，遂成癡也。

translations.literal: ” Liu Cong showed the memorial to Wang Shen and laughed: “Yuanda has turned these boys witless.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Cong flashed the paper at his favourites: “Yuanda has driven them mad.”

sentences.zh: 」寢之。

translations.literal: He tossed it aside.
translations.idiomatic: He shelved the plea.

sentences.zh: 沈等頓首泣曰：「臣等小人，過蒙陛下識拔，幸得備灑掃宮閣，而王公朝士疾臣等如仇讎，又深恨陛下。

translations.literal: They kowtowed weeping: “We are insects whom you raised to sweep palaces—yet lords hate us like foes and curse Your Majesty.”
translations.idiomatic: They sobbed: “We were gutter scraps you lifted—now nobles hunt us and damn your name.”

sentences.zh: 願收大造之恩，以臣等膏之鼎鑊，皇朝上下自然雍穆矣。

translations.literal: Boil us in cauldrons if it restores harmony.”
translations.idiomatic: Cook us alive if peace returns.”

sentences.zh: 」聰曰：「此等狂言恆然，卿復何足恨乎！

translations.literal: ” Liu Cong said: “Mad words mean nothing—why resent them?”
translations.idiomatic: ” He shrugged: “Let them rant.”

sentences.zh: 」更以訪粲，粲盛稱沈等忠清，乃心王室。

translations.literal: He asked Liu Can, who swore Wang Shen’s crew loyal as ice.
translations.idiomatic: He polled Liu Can, who swore the eunuchs pure.

sentences.zh: 聰大悅，封沈為列侯。

translations.literal: Delighted, Liu Cong ennobled Wang Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong joyfully raised Wang Shen to marquis.

sentences.zh: 太宰劉易詣闕，又上疏固諫。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Liu Yi stormed the palace with another plea.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi rushed back with a harder memorial.

sentences.zh: 聰大怒，手壞其表，易遂忿恚而死，元達哭之悲慟，曰：「人之云亡，邦國殄悴。

translations.literal: Liu Cong tore the paper with his bare hands; Yi died of rage while Yuanda wailed: “When wise men perish the state withers.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong shredded it; Liu Yi collapsed dead as Yuanda keened the Book of Songs’ lament.

sentences.zh: 吾既不復能言，安用此默默生乎！

translations.literal: If I may no longer speak, why breathe in silence?
translations.idiomatic: Silenced, why linger alive?”

sentences.zh: 」歸而自殺。

translations.literal: ” He went home and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: ” He retired and opened his veins.

sentences.zh: 北地饑甚，人相食啖，羌酋大軍須運糧以給麹昌，劉雅擊敗之。

translations.literal: Beidi starved until men ate men; a Qiang chief convoyed grain to Qu Chang until Liu Ya smashed him.
translations.idiomatic: Cannibalism swept Beidi when a Qiang chief tried to feed Qu Chang—Liu Ya destroyed the convoy.

sentences.zh: 麹允與劉曜戰于磻石谷，王師敗績，允奔靈武。

translations.literal: Qu Yun fought Liu Yao at Panshi Gorge; imperial troops fled and Yun bolted for Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: At Panshi Gorge Liu Yao shattered Qu Yun’s army and chased him toward Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 平陽大饑，流叛死亡十有五六。

translations.literal: Pingyang’s famine killed or scattered half the people.
translations.idiomatic: Half of Pingyang died or fled the hunger.

sentences.zh: 石勒遣石越率騎二萬，屯於并州，以懷撫叛者。

translations.literal: Shi Le sent Shi Yue with twenty thousand riders to Bingzhou to coax defectors home.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le parked twenty thousand horsemen in Bingzhou to lure refugees back.

sentences.zh: 聰使黃門侍郎喬詩讓勒，勒不奉命，潛結曹嶷，規為鼎峙之勢。

translations.literal: Liu Cong sent Qiao Shi to rebuke him; Shi Le ignored the order and secretly allied with Cao Yi to divide the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Shi’s reprimand failed—Shi Le plotted with Cao Yi for a tripartite standoff.

sentences.zh: 聰立上皇后樊氏，即張氏之侍婢也。

translations.literal: Liu Cong raised chambermaid Fan—once Zhang’s slave—to supreme empress.
translations.idiomatic: He crowned Zhang’s former maid Fan as paramount consort.

sentences.zh: 時四-{后}-之外，佩皇后璽綬者七人，朝廷內外無復綱紀，阿諛日進，貨賄公行，軍旅在外，饑疫相仍，後宮賞賜動至千萬。

translations.literal: Besides four reigning queens seven women bore imperial seals; court discipline vanished; flattery and bribery ruled; armies starved abroad while harem gifts hit millions.
translations.idiomatic: Four official empresses plus seven seal-holders rotted protocol; armies rotted outside while favours splashed millions inside.

sentences.zh: 劉敷屢泣言之，聰不納，怒曰：「爾欲得使汝公死乎？

translations.literal: Liu Fu pleaded until Liu Cong snarled: “Do you wish your father dead?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fu’s tears bought only rage: “Want your prince buried?”

sentences.zh: 朝朝夕夕生來哭人！

translations.literal: Must you wail at me morning and night?”
translations.idiomatic: Must you nag like mourners?”

sentences.zh: 」敷憂忿發病而死。

translations.literal: ” Liu Fu sickened with grief and died.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Fu wasted away and died.

sentences.zh: 河東大蝗，唯不食黍豆。

translations.literal: Locusts swarmed Hedong yet spared millet and beans.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong locusts devoured everything except millet and beans.

sentences.zh: 靳准率部人收而埋之，哭聲聞于十餘里，後乃鑽土飛出，復食黍豆。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun buried them; wailing carried ten li until they burst from the soil to feast again.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun interred the clouds of insects; keening rolled ten li until they tore free and fed.

sentences.zh: 平陽饑甚，司隸部人奔于冀州二十萬戶，石越招之故也。

translations.literal: Two hundred thousand metropolitan households fled famine for Jizhou because Shi Yue beckoned.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred thousand households crossed into Jizhou answering Shi Yue’s call.

sentences.zh: 犬與豕交于相國府門，又交于宮門，又交司隸、御史門。

translations.literal: Dogs mounted sows at the minister’s gate, the palace gate, and the censor’s gate.
translations.idiomatic: Canine and swine coupled before Liu Can’s doors, the palace, and the inspectors.

sentences.zh: 有豕著進賢冠，升聰坐。

translations.literal: A pig donned a scholar’s cap and climbed Liu Cong’s throne.
translations.idiomatic: A hog crowned itself scholar-official and mounted the throne.

sentences.zh: 犬冠武冠，帶綬，與豕並升。

translations.literal: A dog in marshal’s cap and ribbons rose beside it.
translations.idiomatic: A dog in warrior cap and sash joined it.

sentences.zh: 俄而鬥死殿上。

translations.literal: Moments later both lay dead on the dais.
translations.idiomatic: They tore each other dead upon the hall.

sentences.zh: 宿衛莫有見其入者。

translations.literal: Guards saw nothing enter.
translations.idiomatic: No sentry witnessed their entrance.

sentences.zh: 而聰昏虐愈甚，無誡懼之心。

translations.literal: Yet Liu Cong grew crueler and feared nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Still Liu Cong sank deeper into tyranny without dread.

sentences.zh: 宴群臣於光極前殿，引見其太弟乂，容貌毀悴，鬢髮蒼然，涕泣陳謝。

translations.literal: At a Guangji banquet he called Liu Yi forward—gaunt, grey, weeping apologies.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted ministers while Liu Yi stood broken-haired and begging forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 聰亦對之悲慟，縱酒極歡，待之如初。

translations.literal: Liu Cong wept with him, drank wildly, and embraced him as before.
translations.idiomatic: They sobbed together, then drank deep as if nothing had changed.

sentences.zh: 劉曜陷長安外城，湣帝使侍中宋敞送箋於曜，帝肉袒牽羊，輿櫬銜璧出降。

translations.literal: Liu Yao breached Chang’an’s outer wall; Emperor Min sent Song Chang with a letter of surrender—bare-chested, leading a sheep, coffin-laden cart, jade between his teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Song Chang carried Emperor Min’s surrender: the sovereign stripped, sheep-led, coffin before him, seal in mouth.

sentences.zh: 及至平陽，聰以帝為光祿大夫、懷安侯，使粲告於太廟，大赦境內，改年麟嘉。

translations.literal: At Pingyang Liu Cong named him Household Rapid grandee and Marquis of Huai’an; Liu Can announced it at the temple; amnesty followed and the era became Linjia.
translations.idiomatic: In Pingyang Liu Cong titled him minister and marquis, Liu Can burned the news at the shrine, amnesty rang out, and the calendar read Linjia.

sentences.zh: 麹允自殺。

translations.literal: Qu Yun killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun fell on his sword.

sentences.zh: 聰東宮四門無故自壞，後內史女人化為丈夫。

translations.literal: The heir’s four gates collapsed untouched and female clerks sprouted beards.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern palace gates fell alone while women officials grew male whiskers.

sentences.zh: 時聰子約死，一指猶暖，遂不殯殮。

translations.literal: When prince Yue died one fingertip stayed warm, so Liu Cong delayed burial.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue’s finger still pulsed—Liu Cong refused the coffin.

sentences.zh: 及蘇，言見元海於不周山，經五日，遂復從至昆侖山，三日而復返於不周，見諸王公卿將相死者悉在，宮室甚壯麗，號曰蒙珠離國。

translations.literal: Revived, Yue described Mount Buzhou where Liu Yuan waited five days before touring Kunlun three days—every dead lord feasted in mansions called Mengzhuli.
translations.idiomatic: He woke describing Liu Yuan on Buzhou, five days’ march to Kunlun, returning to halls named Mengzhuli crowded with fallen kings.

sentences.zh: 元海謂約曰：「東北有遮須夷國，無主久，待汝父為之。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan told him: “Northeast lies Zhexu Barbaria—kingless—awaiting your father.”
translations.idiomatic: “Zhexu eastward lacks a king—your father will fill it.”

sentences.zh: 汝父後三年當來，來後國中大亂相殺害，吾家死亡略盡，但可永明輩十數人在耳。

translations.literal: “Three years hence he arrives; then our house slaughter one another until barely a dozen Yongming princes survive.”
translations.idiomatic: “He comes in three years—after that kin butcher kin until a handful of Yongming sons remain.”

sentences.zh: 汝且還，後年當來，見汝不久。

translations.literal: “Return now; next year we meet again.”
translations.idiomatic: “Go home—we reunite soon.”

sentences.zh: 」約拜辭而歸，道遇一國曰猗尼渠余國，引約入宮，與約皮囊一枚，曰：「為吾遺漢皇帝。

translations.literal: ” Bowing farewell he met Yiniquyu; its king led him inside, handed a leather satchel: “Give this to Han’s emperor.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Homeward he entered Yiniquyu; its sovereign gave a pouch for Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 」約辭而歸，謂約曰：「劉郎後年來必見過，當以小女相妻。

translations.literal: ” Leaving, the king added: “Lord Liu must visit next year—I offer my daughter.”
translations.idiomatic: ” At the gate the king promised his daughter when Liu returned.

sentences.zh: 」約歸，置皮囊於機上。

translations.literal: ” Yue placed the pouch on his couch.
translations.idiomatic: ” He laid the pouch by his couch.

sentences.zh: 俄而蘇，使左右機上取皮囊開之，有一方白玉，題文曰：「猗尼渠余國天王敬信遮須夷國天王，歲在攝提，當相見也。

translations.literal: Awaking, he opened it to find white jade inscribed: “The celestial king of Yiniquyu honours Zhexu’s king—we meet in the Sheti year.”
translations.idiomatic: Alive again he found jade declaring kings would meet in Sheti year.

sentences.zh: 」馳使呈聰，聰曰：「若審如此，吾不懼死也。

translations.literal: ” Messengers showed Liu Cong, who said: “If fate speaks true I no longer fear death.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Cong smiled: “Then mortality holds no terror.”

sentences.zh: 」及聰死，與此玉並葬焉。

translations.literal: ” When he died they buried the stone with him.
translations.idiomatic: ” The talisman joined him in the tomb.

sentences.zh: 時東宮鬼哭；

translations.literal: Ghosts wept in the eastern palace;
translations.idiomatic: Spirits keened through the heir’s halls;

sentences.zh: 赤虹經天，南有一歧；

translations.literal: a scarlet rainbow split southward;
translations.idiomatic: a blood rainbow forked toward the south;

sentences.zh: 三日並照，各有兩珥，五色甚鮮；

translations.literal: three suns shared the sky, each double-haloed in brilliant hues;
translations.idiomatic: triple suns glared with paired coronae;

sentences.zh: 客星曆紫宮入於天獄而滅。

translations.literal: a stray star crossed the Purple Palace into the Prison constellation and died.
translations.idiomatic: a wanderer star sliced the throne stars into the celestial jail.

sentences.zh: 太史令康相言於聰曰：「蛇虹見彌天，一歧南徹；

translations.literal: Astrologer Kang Xiang warned: “Serpent rainbows span heaven with a southern spur;
translations.idiomatic: Kang Xiang said: “Rainbows coil sky-wide—

sentences.zh: 三日並照；

translations.literal: three suns blaze together;
translations.idiomatic: three suns clash—

sentences.zh: 客星入紫宮。

translations.literal: guest stars pierce the throne.”
translations.idiomatic: omens assault the Purple Palace.”

sentences.zh: 此皆大異，其徵不遠也。

translations.literal: Such prodigies strike soon.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster follows swiftly.

sentences.zh: 今虹達東西者，許洛以南不可圖也。

translations.literal: Rainbows east-to-west mean south of Xu–Luo will never yield.
translations.idiomatic: The arc from Xu to Luo bars conquest southward.

sentences.zh: 一歧南徹者，李氏當仍跨巴蜀，司馬睿終據全吳之象，天下其三分乎！

translations.literal: The southern spur shows Li Xiong holding Ba–Shu while Sima Rui masters Wu—the realm splits three ways.”
translations.idiomatic: The southern fork marks Li clan in Shu and Sima Rui in Wu—tripartite empire.”

sentences.zh: 月為胡王，皇漢雖苞括二京，龍騰九五，然世雄燕代，肇基北朔，太陰之變其在漢域乎！

translations.literal: The moon rules barbarian kings; though Han seized both capitals and mounts the nine-five, its heroes hail from Yan–Dai—Great Yin’s change lands here.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar omens favour northern khans—Han may wear the crown yet Yin’s curse stalks Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 漢既據中原，曆命所屬，紫宮之異，亦不在他，此之深重，胡可盡言。

translations.literal: Han holds the Central Plain by mandate—Purple Palace omens target none other; words cannot exhaust their weight.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven points at us alone—the palace stars convict our house.

sentences.zh: 石勒鴟視趙魏，曹嶷狼顧東齊，鮮卑之眾星布燕代，齊、代、燕、趙皆有將大之氣。

translations.literal: Shi Le glares from Zhao–Wei; Cao Yi eyes Qi; Xianbei scatter like stars across Yan–Dai—every northern march smells of empire.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le circles Zhao–Wei; Cao Yi prowls Qi; Xianbei blanket Yan–Dai—greatness stirs on every frontier.

sentences.zh: 願陛下以東夏為慮，勿顧西南。

translations.literal: Fix your gaze on the eastern Xia—forget the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Secure the east—ignore Bashu.

sentences.zh: 吳蜀之不能北侵，猶大漢之不能南向也。

translations.literal: Wu and Shu cannot march north any more than we can swallow south.”
translations.idiomatic: They cannot strike northward—nor can we march south.”

sentences.zh: 今京師寡弱，勒眾精盛，若盡趙魏之銳，燕之突騎自上黨而來，曹嶷率三齊之眾以繼之，陛下將何以抗之？

translations.literal: The capital is weak while Shi Le’s host is elite—if he mobilises Zhao–Wei, Yan’s raiders strike from Shangdang, and Cao Yi drives Qi behind him—how will you resist?
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang stands naked against Shi Le’s veterans; Xianbei could sweep from Shangdang while Cao Yi raises Qi—how do you answer that hammer?’

sentences.zh: 紫宮之變何必不在此乎！

translations.literal: Need not the Purple Palace omen fall here?
translations.idiomatic: Does not the throne-star warn of just such a storm?’

sentences.zh: 願陛下早為之所，無使兆人生心。

translations.literal: Act before the people lose heart.
translations.idiomatic: Move before the mob reads doom in the sky.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能發詔，外以遠追秦皇、漢武循海之事，內為高帝圖楚之計，無不克矣。

translations.literal: Issue an edict: outwardly mimic Qin Shi Huang and Han Wu patrolling the seas; inwardly plot Gaozu’s strangulation of Chu—nothing will withstand you.
translations.idiomatic: March coastal roads like the First Emperor, throttle foes like Han Gaozu choking Xiang Yu—victory follows.

sentences.zh: 」聰覽之不悅。

translations.literal: Liu Cong read the memorial with a scowl.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tossed the paper aside, furious.

sentences.zh: 劉粲使王平謂劉乂曰：「適奉中詔，云京師將有變，敕裹甲以備之。

translations.literal: Liu Can sent Wang Ping to Liu Yi: “An inner edict warns of unrest in the capital—arm yourselves.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ping arrived whispering palace orders to strip for battle.

sentences.zh: 」乂以為信然，令命宮臣裹甲以居。

translations.literal: Yi believed him and ordered every eastern-palace officer into armour.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi trusted the tale and mobilised his household corps.

sentences.zh: 粲馳遣告靳准、王沈等曰：「向也王平告云東宮陰備非常，將若之何？

translations.literal: Can galloped to Jin Zhun and Wang Shen: “Wang Ping says the heir plots—what now?”
translations.idiomatic: He raced to the eunuchs: “The heir arms for coup.”

sentences.zh: 」准白之，聰大驚曰：「豈有此乎！

translations.literal: Zhun reported it; Liu Cong cried: “Can this be?”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gasped when Zhun repeated it.

sentences.zh: 」王沈等同聲曰：「臣等久聞，但恐言之陛下弗信。

translations.literal: Wang Shen chorused: “We long knew yet feared you would not believe.”
translations.idiomatic: The favourites moaned they had whispered truth for years.

sentences.zh: 」於是使粲圍東宮。

translations.literal: Liu Can ringed the eastern palace.
translations.idiomatic: Household troops surrounded Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 粲遣沈、准收氐羌酋長十餘人，窮問之，皆懸首高格，燒鐵灼目，乃自誣與乂同造逆謀。

translations.literal: He sent Shen and Zhun to seize Di and Qiang chiefs, rack them with hooks and branding irons until they confessed sedition with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: They tortured tribal leaders until they framed Liu Yi under glowing iron.

sentences.zh: 聰謂沈等言曰：「而今而後，吾知卿等忠於朕也。

translations.literal: Liu Cong told them: “Now I see your loyalty.”
translations.idiomatic: He embraced the torturers as patriots.

sentences.zh: 當念為知無不言，勿恨往日言不用也。

translations.literal: Speak everything hereafter—do not brood on ignored counsel.”
translations.idiomatic: Hold nothing back—I heed you now.”

sentences.zh: 」於是誅乂素所親厚大臣及東宮官屬數十人，皆靳准及閹豎所怨也。

translations.literal: He executed dozens of Yi’s ministers and household—all enemies of Zhun and the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Blades fell on every friend Liu Yi had left.

sentences.zh: 廢乂為北部王，粲使准賊殺之。

translations.literal: Yi was demoted Prince of the North; Zhun murdered him by night.
translations.idiomatic: They stripped him to “Prince of the North” before Jin Zhun cut his throat.

sentences.zh: 坑士眾萬五千餘人，平陽街巷為之空。

translations.literal: Fifteen thousand soldiers went into common graves; Pingyang’s lanes emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Mass graves swallowed fifteen thousand guards; the capital fell silent.

sentences.zh: 氏羌叛者十餘萬落，以靳准行車騎大將軍以討之。

translations.literal: Hundreds of thousands of Di and Qiang rose; Liu Cong named Jin Zhun field marshal to crush them.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious tribes mustered ten thousand camps—Jin Zhun rode against them.

sentences.zh: 時聰境內大蝗，平陽、冀、雍尤甚。

translations.literal: Locusts devoured Liu Cong’s realm—worst in Pingyang, Ji, and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Swarms gnawed Pingyang, Ji, and Yong bare.

sentences.zh: 靳准討之，震其二子而死。

translations.literal: When Zhun campaigned lightning killed two of his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Lightning struck Jin Zhun’s sons dead on campaign.

sentences.zh: 河汾大溢，漂沒千餘家。

translations.literal: The Fen and Fen tributaries burst and drowned a thousand homes.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow River floods erased riverside hamlets.

sentences.zh: 東宮災異，門閣宮殿蕩然。

translations.literal: Fire and prodigies stripped the eastern palace gates and halls bare.
translations.idiomatic: Portents razed the heir’s towers to shells.

sentences.zh: 立粲為皇太子，大赦殊死已下。

translations.literal: He named Liu Can heir and proclaimed amnesty short of death.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can took the heir’s seal amid general pardon.

sentences.zh: 以粲領相國、大單于，總攝朝政如前。

translations.literal: Can kept minister of state and great Chanyu titles and ruled as before.
translations.idiomatic: He retained ministerial and Chanyu powers unchanged.

sentences.zh: 聰校獵上林，以帝行車騎將軍，戎服執戟前導，行三驅之禮。

translations.literal: Liu Cong hunted Shanglin Park forcing Emperor Min to march as chariot general in armour with halberd—performing the three-sided hunt ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He humiliated Emperor Min as herald for a royal hunt.

sentences.zh: 粲言於聰曰：「今司馬氏跨據江東，趙固、李矩同逆相濟，興兵聚眾者皆以子鄴為名，不如除之，以絕其望。

translations.literal: Can urged: “Sima clan holds Jiangdong; Zhao Gu and Li Ju aid each other—every rebel banner cries ‘restore Ye’—kill the captive to silence them.”
translations.idiomatic: He argued executing Emperor Min would break Jin morale.

sentences.zh: 」聰然之。

translations.literal: Liu Cong agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded.

sentences.zh: 趙固郭默攻其河東，至於絳邑，右司隸部人盜牧馬負妻子奔之者三萬餘騎。

translations.literal: Zhao Gu and Gu Mo struck Hedong to Jiangyi; thirty thousand families stole horses and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty thousand households bolted east with stolen mounts.

sentences.zh: 騎兵將軍劉勳追討之，殺萬餘人，固、默引歸。

translations.literal: Liu Xun chased them, killed ten thousand, and drove Zhao Gu home.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry commander Liu Xun butchered ten thousand before the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 劉頡遮邀擊之，為固所敗。

translations.literal: Liu Jie ambushed them and fell to Zhao Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jie’s ambush collapsed.

sentences.zh: 使粲及劉雅等伐趙固，次於小平津，固揚言曰：「要當生縛劉粲以贖天子。

translations.literal: Liu Can and Liu Ya marched on Zhao Gu, halted at Xiaoping Ford; Gu swore to bind Liu Can alive and ransom the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaoping Ford Zhao Gu vowed to cage Liu Can.

sentences.zh: 」聰聞而惡之。

translations.literal: The boast enraged Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong seethed at the insult.

sentences.zh: 李矩使郭默、郭誦救趙固，屯於洛汭，遣耿稚、張皮潛濟，襲粲。

translations.literal: Li Ju sent Gu Mo and Gu Song with Geng Zhi and Zhang Pi to ford secretly and strike Liu Can.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju’s captains crossed by night to stab Liu Can.

sentences.zh: 貝丘王翼光自厘城覘之，以告粲。

translations.literal: Prince Wang Yiguang spied from Licheng and warned Liu Can.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yiguang rode from Licheng with intelligence.

sentences.zh: 粲曰：「征北南渡，趙固望聲逃竄，彼方憂自固，何暇來邪！

translations.literal: Liu Can sneered: “The northern army fled south—Zhao Gu hugs his walls—why fear a raid?
translations.idiomatic: He mocked: “Zhao Gu hides—who attacks?”

sentences.zh: 且聞上身在此，自當不敢北視，況敢濟乎！

translations.literal: With me here they dare not even glance north—much less ford!”
translations.idiomatic: “Father camps nearby—they would not cross!”

sentences.zh: 不須驚動將士也。

translations.literal: Do not disturb the troops.”
translations.idiomatic: Stand down.”

sentences.zh: 」是夜，稚等襲敗粲軍，粲奔據陽鄉，稚館穀粲壘。

translations.literal: That night Geng Zhi shattered Liu Can’s camp; Can fled to Yangxiang while Geng fed his men from Liu’s stores.
translations.idiomatic: Night fell and Geng Zhi routed him; Liu Can bolted to Yangxiang starving his foe on captured grain.

sentences.zh: 雅聞而馳還，柵於壘外，與稚相持。

translations.literal: Liu Ya raced back and fenced Geng outside the ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ya threw palisades around Geng Zhi.

sentences.zh: 聰聞粲敗，使太尉范隆率騎赴之，稚等懼，率眾五千，突圍趨北山而南。

translations.literal: Hearing of Can’s rout Liu Cong sent Fan Long; Geng broke out with five thousand toward the northern hills.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Long’s rescue terrified Geng into a breakout.

sentences.zh: 劉勳追之，戰于河陽，稚師大敗，死者三千五百人，投河死者千餘人。

translations.literal: Liu Xun ran them down at Heyang—3,500 dead on the field, over a thousand drowned.
translations.idiomatic: At Heyang Liu Xun drowned and hacked thirty-five hundred.

sentences.zh: 聰所居螽斯則百堂災，焚其子會稽王衷已下二十有一人。

translations.literal: Fire consumed Liu Cong’s Zhongsi hall and twenty-one princes including Prince Ai of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Flames devoured twenty-one royal sons from Liu Ai downward.

sentences.zh: 聰聞之，自投於床，哀塞氣絕，良久乃蘇。

translations.literal: Liu Cong collapsed on his couch breathless until aides revived him.
translations.idiomatic: He fell senseless on the bed.

sentences.zh: 平陽西明門牡自亡，霍山崩。

translations.literal: Pingyang’s western brightness gate lost its bolts and Mount Huo collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: West Gate bolts vanished while Huoshan mountain fell.

sentences.zh: 署其驃騎大將軍、濟南王劉驥為大將軍、都督中外諸軍事、錄尚書，衛大將軍、齊王劉勱為大司徒。

translations.literal: He appointed Cavalry Marshal Liu Ji of Jinan grand marshal and overseer of all armies with recording powers, and Guard Marshal Liu Mai of Qi grand steward.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji became commander-in-chief; Liu Mai took the steward’s seal.

sentences.zh: 中常侍王沈養女年十四，有妙色，聰立為左皇后。

translations.literal: Wang Shen’s fourteen-year-old foster daughter—ravishing—became left empress.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong crowned Wang Shen’s teenage ward left empress.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王鑒、中書監崔懿之、中書令曹恂等諫曰：「臣聞王者之立-{后}-也，將以上配乾坤之性，象二儀敷育之義，生承宗廟，母臨天下，亡配后土，執饋皇姑，必擇世德名宗，幽閒淑令，副四海之望，稱神祇之心。

translations.literal: Director Wang Jian, palace supervisor Cui Yizhi, and palace secretary Cao Xun pleaded: “Kings choose queens to mate Heaven and Earth, mother the realm, serve ancestresses, and anchor sacrifice—only noble virtue satisfies gods and men.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers cited ritual: empresses mirror cosmos—they must spring from titled houses.

sentences.zh: 是故周文造舟，姒氏以興，《關雎》之化饗，則百世之祚永。

translations.literal: King Wen’s barges raised the Si clan; the lessons of “Guanju” blessed Zhou for ages.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou rose on royal marriages praised in the Odes.

sentences.zh: 孝成任心縱欲，以婢為-{后}-，使皇統亡絕，社稷淪傾。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng followed lust and raised a maid—cutting the succession and toppling the altars.
translations.idiomatic: Han Chengdi’s slave-born empress ended his line.

sentences.zh: 有周之隆既如彼矣，大漢之禍又如此矣。

translations.literal: Zhou flourished thus; Han fell thus.
translations.idiomatic: Glory and ruin teach the same lesson.

sentences.zh: 從麟嘉以來，亂淫於色，縱沈之弟女，刑余小丑猶不可塵瓊寢，汙清廟，況其家婢邪！

translations.literal: Since Linjia you wallow in flesh—even Wang Shen’s niece, a scarred puppet, must not foul the jade bed—how much less a household slave!
translations.idiomatic: Since Linjia lust rules—you stain the shrine with eunuchs’ kin—never a chambermaid queen!

sentences.zh: 六宮妃嬪皆公子公孫，奈何一旦以婢主之，何異象榱玉簀而對腐木朽楹哉！

translations.literal: Six palaces hold lordly daughters—how crown a servant—what else but pairing ivory beams with rotten pillars?
translations.idiomatic: Noblewomen fill the harem—elevating maids mocks timber with termites.

sentences.zh: 臣恐無福於國家也。

translations.literal: We fear no blessing will touch the throne.”
translations.idiomatic: No fortune attends such matches.”

sentences.zh: 」聰覽之大怒，使宣懷謂粲曰：「鑒等小子，慢侮國家，狂言自口，無復君臣上下之禮，其速考竟。

translations.literal: Liu Cong raged and told Liu Can via Xuan Huai: “Jian insults the court—gag them forever.”
translations.idiomatic: He ordered summary execution for the memorialists.

sentences.zh: 」於是收鑒等送市。

translations.literal: Guards dragged Jian’s party to the market.
translations.idiomatic: They chained Wang Jian’s circle for beheading.

sentences.zh: 金紫光祿大夫王延馳將入諫，門者弗通。

translations.literal: Wang Yan galloped to protest but gatekeepers barred him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan never reached the throne hall.

sentences.zh: 鑒等臨刑，王沈以杖叩之曰：「庸奴，復能為惡乎？

translations.literal: At the block Wang Shen tapped Wang Jian with a cane: “Slave—plot again?”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen mocked the condemned.

sentences.zh: 乃公何與汝事！

translations.literal: What has your father to do with you!”
translations.idiomatic: Old fool—what’s your grudge?”

sentences.zh: 」鑒瞋目叱之曰：「豎子！

translations.literal: Jian glared: “Brat!”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian spat back.

sentences.zh: 使皇漢滅者，坐汝鼠輩與靳准耳，要當訴汝於先帝，取汝等於地下。

translations.literal: Han falls on rats like you and Jin Zhun—I will indict you before the late emperor.”
translations.idiomatic: You and Zhun murdered Han—I’ll sue you underground.”

sentences.zh: 」懿之曰：「靳准梟聲鏡形，必為國患。

translations.literal: Cui Yizhi added: “Jin Zhun’s face prophesies rebellion.”
translations.idiomatic: Cui called Zhun a born traitor.

sentences.zh: 汝既食人，人亦當食汝。

translations.literal: You feed on men—men will feed on you.”
translations.idiomatic: Cannibals feast last.”

sentences.zh: 」皆斬之。

translations.literal: All were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Axes fell.

sentences.zh: 聰又立其中常侍宣懷養女為中皇后。

translations.literal: Liu Cong raised Xuan Huai’s foster daughter as central empress.
translations.idiomatic: Another maid-queen followed—Xuan Huai’s ward.

sentences.zh: 鬼哭於光極殿，又哭於建始殿。

translations.literal: Ghosts wailed in Guangji and Jianshi halls.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits keened through twin throne rooms.

sentences.zh: 雨血平陽，廣袤十里。

translations.literal: Blood rain soaked ten li of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Red rain slicked ten li around the capital.

sentences.zh: 時聰子約已死，至是晝見。

translations.literal: Prince Yue, long dead, appeared in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: Dead Prince Yue walked under the sun.

sentences.zh: 聰甚惡之，謂粲曰：「吾寢疾惙頓，怪異特甚。

translations.literal: Horrified, Liu Cong told Liu Can: “Illness wracks me—omens multiply.
translations.idiomatic: He confessed dread to Liu Can.

sentences.zh: 往以約之言為妖，比累日見之，此兒必來迎吾也。

translations.literal: I mocked Yue’s vision—now daily sightings prove he comes for me.”
translations.idiomatic: Visions vindicate my dead son’s prophecy.

sentences.zh: 何圖人死定有神靈，如是，吾不悲死也。

translations.literal: If death truly harbours spirits I no longer mourn dying.”
translations.idiomatic: Spirits mean peace—I fear nothing.

sentences.zh: 今世難未夷，非諒暗之日，朝終夕殮，旬日而葬。

translations.literal: War forbids lengthy mourning—bury me within ten days from dusk to dawn.”
translations.idiomatic: No lengthy vigil—wrap me within ten days.

sentences.zh: 」徵劉曜為丞相、錄尚書，輔政，固辭乃止。

translations.literal: He summoned Liu Yao as chancellor until Liu Yao refused.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao declined the regency.

sentences.zh: 仍以劉景為太宰，劉驥為大司馬，劉顗為太師，朱紀為太傅，呼延晏為太保，並錄尚書事；

translations.literal: Liu Jing stayed grand tutor, Liu Ji grand marshal, Liu Yi grand preceptor, Zhu Ji grand tutor, Huyan Yan grand guardian—all recording ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Seven Seniors divided seals among Liu Jing, Liu Ji, Liu Yi, Zhu Ji, and Huyan Yan.

sentences.zh: 范隆守尚書令、儀同三司，靳准為大司空、領司隸校尉，皆迭決尚書奏事。

translations.literal: Fan Long kept the director’s chair with ducal honours; Jin Zhun took minister of works and metropolitan command—rotating court verdicts.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Long and Jin Zhun traded judicial duties.

sentences.zh: ，聰死，在位九年，偽諡曰昭武皇帝，廟號烈宗。

translations.literal: Liu Cong died after nine years’ reign, posthumously titled Emperor Zhaowu with temple name Liezong.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years on the throne ended—posthumous Emperor Zhaowu, temple Liezong.

sentences.zh: 劉粲

translations.literal: Liu Can.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can.

sentences.zh: 粲字士光。

translations.literal: Courtesy name Shiguang.
translations.idiomatic: His style was Shiguang.

sentences.zh: 少而俊傑，才兼文武。

translations.literal: Youth brought heroic talent in both civil and military arts.
translations.idiomatic: Brilliant in brush and blade.

sentences.zh: 自為宰相，威福任情，疏遠忠賢，昵近奸佞，任性嚴刻無恩惠，距諫飾非。

translations.literal: As minister he wielded whim like law—spurned worthies, cuddled knaves, punished harshly, silenced counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Power turned him cruel and deaf to truth.

sentences.zh: 好興造宮室，相國之府仿像紫宮，在位無幾，作兼晝夜，饑困窮叛，死亡相繼，粲弗之恤也。

translations.literal: He raised mansions rivalling the Purple Palace, labouring day and night until famine and revolt stacked corpses he ignored.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces rose while peasants starved—he shrugged.

sentences.zh: 既嗣偽位，尊聰-{后}-靳氏為皇太后，樊氏號弘道皇后，宣氏號弘德皇后，王氏號弘孝皇后。

translations.literal: Once emperor he honoured Dowager Jin, titled Fan Hongdao queen, Xuan Hongde queen, Wang Hongxiao queen.
translations.idiomatic: He crowned three dowagers—Jin, Fan, Xuan, Wang—with flowery titles.

sentences.zh: 靳等年皆未滿二十，並國色也，粲晨夜蒸淫於內，志不在哀。

translations.literal: None yet twenty and peerless beauties—he debauched them nightly instead of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Teen consorts filled his bed while kin lay unburied.

sentences.zh: 立其妻靳氏為皇后，子元公為太子，大赦境內，改元漢昌。

translations.literal: He named Lady Jin empress, son Yuangong heir, amnesty, era Hanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jin became empress; Prince Yuangong heir; era Hanchang.

sentences.zh: 雨血於平陽。

translations.literal: Blood rain fell on Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Red rain washed Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 靳準將有異謀，私於粲曰：「如聞諸公將欲行伊尹、霍光之事，謀先誅太保及臣，以大司馬統萬機。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun whispered: “Nobles plot Yi Yin’s coup—murder the grand guardian and me so the grand marshal rules.”
translations.idiomatic: He invented a Huo Guang conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 陛下若不先之，臣恐禍之來也不晨則夕。

translations.literal: Strike first or doom strikes by dusk.”
translations.idiomatic: Move before dusk.”

sentences.zh: 」粲弗納。

translations.literal: Liu Can dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can laughed it off.

sentences.zh: 准懼其言之不從，謂聰二靳氏曰：「今諸公侯欲廢帝，立濟南王，恐吾家無復種矣。

translations.literal: Zhun frightened two Jin ladies: “Lords mean to topple the throne for Prince Jinan—our clan dies rootless.”
translations.idiomatic: He panicked the Jin concubines.

sentences.zh: 盍言之於帝。

translations.literal: Speak to His Majesty.”
translations.idiomatic: Tell the emperor.”

sentences.zh: 」二靳承間言之。

translations.literal: They pleaded during intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: They whispered in bed.

sentences.zh: 粲誅其太宰、上洛王劉景，太師、昌國公劉顗，大司馬、濟南王劉驥，大司徒、齊王劉勱等。

translations.literal: Liu Can executed Grand Tutor Liu Jing of Shangluo, Grand Preceptor Liu Yi of Changguo, Grand Marshal Liu Ji of Jinan, Grand Steward Liu Mai of Qi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Blades fell on Liu Jing, Liu Yi, Liu Ji, Liu Mai.

sentences.zh: 太傅朱紀、太尉范隆出奔長安。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Zhu Ji and Grand Commandant Fan Long fled to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ji and Fan Long bolted west.

sentences.zh: 又誅其車騎大將軍、吳王劉逞，驥母弟也。

translations.literal: He killed Prince Cheng of Wu—Liu Ji’s brother.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wu Liu Cheng died next.

sentences.zh: 粲大閱上林，謀討石勒。

translations.literal: Liu Can reviewed troops at Shanglin plotting against Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled at Shanglin to face Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 以靳准為大將軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun became grand general with recording powers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun took marshal and recorder titles.

sentences.zh: 粲荒耽酒色，遊宴後庭，軍國之事一決於准。

translations.literal: Liu Can drowned in wine and flesh while Jin Zhun ruled.
translations.idiomatic: Banquets hid Zhun’s dictatorship.

sentences.zh: 准矯粲命，以從弟明為車騎將軍，康為衛將軍。

translations.literal: Zhun forged orders naming cousins Ming and Kang chariot and guard generals.
translations.idiomatic: Forged edicts promoted his cousins.

sentences.zh: 準將作亂，以金紫光祿大夫王延耆德時望，謀之於延。

translations.literal: Plotting coup he sounded Wang Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He sounded elder Wang Yan.

sentences.zh: 延弗從，馳將告之，遇靳康，劫延以歸。

translations.literal: Yan refused and raced to warn Liu Can but Jin Kang seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan ran to alert the throne until Kang kidnapped him.

sentences.zh: 准勒兵入宮，升其光極前殿，下使甲士執粲，數而殺之。

translations.literal: Zhun stormed Guangji Hall, chained Liu Can, pronounced his crimes, and slew him.
translations.idiomatic: Armoured guards dragged Liu Can from the throne and killed him.

sentences.zh: 劉氏男女無少長皆斬於東市。

translations.literal: Liu clansmen—every age—were executed in the eastern marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Every Liu—child or elder—died on the eastern block.

sentences.zh: 發掘元海、聰墓，焚燒其宗廟。

translations.literal: They dug up Liu Yuan’s and Liu Cong’s tombs and burned the ancestral shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels opened the royal graves and torched the temples.

sentences.zh: 鬼大哭，聲聞百里。

translations.literal: Spirits howled loud enough to carry a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Wailing ghosts shook the countryside for miles.

sentences.zh: 准自號大將軍、漢天王，置百官，遣使稱籓于晉。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun styled himself grand marshal and Heavenly King of Han, appointed a full bureaucracy, and sent envoys offering vassalage to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun crowned himself Han’s warrior-king, staffed a court, and sued Jin for recognition.

sentences.zh: 左光祿劉雅出奔西平。

translations.literal: Household Rapid Liu Ya fled toward Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ya bolted for Xiping.

sentences.zh: 尚書北宮純、胡崧等招集晉人，保于東宮，靳康攻滅之。

translations.literal: Director Bei Gong Chun and Hu Song rallied Jin loyalists in the eastern palace until Jin Kang wiped them out.
translations.idiomatic: Bei Gong Chun and Hu Song held the heir’s compound until Zhun’s cousin stormed it.

sentences.zh: 準將以王延為左光祿，延罵曰：「屠各逆奴，何不速殺我，以吾左目置西陽門，觀相國之入也，右目置建春門，觀大將軍之入也。

translations.literal: When Zhun offered Wang Yan the Household Rapid portfolio Yan cursed: “Tuge slave—kill me now; hang my left eye on West Yang Gate to watch your minister enter and my right on Jianchun Gate to watch your marshal.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan spat at the Tuge rebel: “Murder me—let my eyes witness your triumphal entries.”

sentences.zh: 」准怒，殺之。

translations.literal: Enraged, Zhun executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun cut him down.

sentences.zh: 陳元達

translations.literal: Chen Yuanda.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuanda.

sentences.zh: 陳元達，字長宏，後部人也。

translations.literal: Chen Yuanda, courtesy name Changhong, came from the Rear Division.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuanda (style Changhong) hailed from the Rear Division tribes.

sentences.zh: 本姓高，以生月妨父，故改云陳。

translations.literal: His clan had been Gao; because his birth month was deemed harmful to his father he adopted Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Born under an ill omen for his father, he forsook the surname Gao for Chen.

sentences.zh: 少面孤貧，常躬耕兼誦書，樂道行詠，忻忻如也。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor, he farmed with his own hands yet memorised texts, chanting the Way as he walked—always content.
translations.idiomatic: He hoed fields by day and books by night, humming verses—happy in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 至年四十，不與人交通。

translations.literal: Until forty he mingled with no one.
translations.idiomatic: At forty he still kept to himself.

sentences.zh: 元海之為左賢王，聞而招之，元達不答。

translations.literal: When Liu Yuan became Wise King of the Left he summoned Yuanda, who ignored the call.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan’s first summons went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 及元海僭號，人謂元達曰：「往劉公相屈，君蔑而不顧，今稱號龍飛，君其懼乎？

translations.literal: After Liu Yuan seized the imperial style men taunted Yuanda: “You snubbed him as lord—now the dragon flies—are you frightened?”
translations.idiomatic: Friends sneered when Liu Yuan took the throne: “Still too proud to answer?”

sentences.zh: 」元達笑曰：「是何言邪？

translations.literal: Yuanda laughed: “What nonsense is that?
translations.idiomatic: He laughed: “Nonsense.

sentences.zh: 彼人姿度卓犖，有籠羅宇宙之志，吾固知之久矣。

translations.literal: His bearing towers above others and his heart nets the cosmos—I have known it long.”
translations.idiomatic: That man aims to rope heaven and earth—I saw it years ago.”

sentences.zh: 然往日所以不往者，以期運未至，不能無事喧喧，彼自有以亮吾矣。

translations.literal: I stayed away because the hour had not struck—I would not clamour without cause—he understands.”
translations.idiomatic: I waited for destiny rather than beg idle posts—he forgives that.”

sentences.zh: 卿但識之，吾恐不過二三日，驛書必至。

translations.literal: Mark my words: within days relay riders will fetch me.”
translations.idiomatic: Watch—the courier comes inside three days.”

sentences.zh: 」其暮，元海果徵元達為黃門郎。

translations.literal: That very evening Liu Yuan appointed him gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: That night the imperial summons arrived naming him a palace gentleman.

sentences.zh: 人曰：「君殆聖乎！

translations.literal: Men exclaimed: “Are you a sage?”
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers gasped: “A prophet!”

sentences.zh: 」既至，引見，元海曰：「卿若早來，豈為郎官而已。

translations.literal: At audience Liu Yuan said: “Had you come sooner you would not be merely a gentleman.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan told him: “Early arrival would have won you higher rank.”

sentences.zh: 」元達曰：「臣惟性之有分，盈分者顛。

translations.literal: Yuanda replied: “Each man has his measure—overflow invites ruin.
translations.idiomatic: “Every bowl has its brim,” Yuanda answered.

sentences.zh: 臣若早叩天門者，恐大王賜處於九卿、納言之間，此則非臣之分，臣將何以堪之！

translations.literal: Had I knocked earlier you might have parked me among the Nine Ministers—beyond my strength to bear.”
translations.idiomatic: “Had I rushed in you might have piled Nine Ministers on my back—I could never lift such weight.”

sentences.zh: 是以抑情盤桓，待分而至，大王無過授之謗，小臣免招寇之禍，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: So I waited until the fit office opened—sparing you blame for excess and myself the envy of rivals—is that not best?”
translations.idiomatic: “So I waited for the right chair—saving you gossip and me assassins.”

sentences.zh: 」元海大悅。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan roared approval.

sentences.zh: 在位忠謇，屢進讜言，退而削草，雖子弟莫得而知也。

translations.literal: In office he served bluntly loyal counsel, burned each draft so even kin never read his words.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke truth and burned his drafts—even family never learned his memos.

sentences.zh: 聰每謂元達曰：「卿當畏朕，反使朕畏卿乎？

translations.literal: Liu Cong often said: “Should you fear me—or must I fear you?”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong teased: “Which of us should tremble?”

sentences.zh: 」元達叩頭謝曰：「臣聞師臣者王，友臣者霸。

translations.literal: Yuanda kowtowed: “A king who treats ministers as teachers reigns; who treats them as friends hegemons.”
translations.idiomatic: “Master your ministers and you rule; befriend them and you dominate.”

sentences.zh: 臣誠愚暗無可采也，幸邀陛下垂齊桓納九九之義，故使微臣得盡愚忠。

translations.literal: Though I am dull, grant me Duke Huan’s ear for every talent—then this fool may prove loyal.”
translations.idiomatic: “Let me be your Guan Zhong—you may yet profit from blunt counsel.”

sentences.zh: 昔世宗遙可汲黯之奏，故能恢隆漢道；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu welcomed Ji An’s memoranda from afar and widened Han’s glory;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu endorsed Ji An’s blunt memorials from afar, Han’s greatness rose again.

sentences.zh: 桀紂誅諫，幽厲弭謗，是以三代之亡也忽焉。

translations.literal: Jie and Zhou slew advisers; You and Li silenced criticism—thus the Three Dynasties fell overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Jie and Zhou murdered counsellors while You and Li smothered dissent—and those dynasties vanished overnight.

sentences.zh: 陛下以大聖應期，挺不世之量，能遠捐商周覆國之弊，近模孝武光漢之美，則天下幸甚，群臣知免。

translations.literal: Your Majesty answers the age as a great sage—reject Shang and Zhou’s ruin, mirror Emperor Wu’s revival—and fortune returns while ministers breathe easier.”
translations.idiomatic: You ride heaven’s mandate—shun Xia’s cruelty, copy Han Wudi’s revival—and we all survive.”

sentences.zh: 」及其死也，人盡冤之。

translations.literal: When he died everyone called it injustice.
translations.idiomatic: His death struck the realm as a crime.
